translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 249

sentences.zh: 【唐紀六十五】起上章敦牂，盡屠維單閼，凡十年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 65] From Shangzhang Dunzang through Tuwéi Danqian; ten years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 65] From Shangzhang Dunzang through Tuwéi Danqian—ten years in all.

sentences.zh: 宣宗元聖至明成武獻文睿智章仁神聰懿道大孝皇帝下大中四年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuānzong, the Yuan, Sheng, Zhi, Ming, Cheng, Wu, Xian, Wen, Rui, Zhi, Zhang, Ren, Shen, Cong, Yi, Dao, Great Filial Emperor (posthumous titles)—below; fourth year of the Dazhong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuānzong (posthumous titles)—the latter part of his reign; fourth year of the Dazhong era (

sentences.zh: 庚午，公元八五零年）

translations.literal: gengwu, corresponding to 850 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengwu, 850 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚辰朔，赦天下。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the gengchen new moon, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the gengchen new moon, the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 二月，以秦州隸鳳翔。

translations.literal: In the second month, Qin Prefecture was placed under the jurisdiction of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Qin Prefecture was placed under Fengxiang's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚戌，以中書侍郎、同平章事馬植為天平節度使。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on gengxu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal Chief Minister Ma Zhi was appointed military commissioner of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengxu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal Chief Minister Ma Zhi was appointed military commissioner of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 上之立也，左軍中尉馬元贄有力焉，由是恩遇冠諸宦者，植與之敘宗姓。

translations.literal: When the emperor was established on the throne, Left Army Commandant Ma Yuanzan had been of great help; thereafter his favor surpassed that of all other eunuchs, and Ma Zhi claimed kinship with him by clan name.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had been enthroned, Left Army Commandant Ma Yuanzan had been instrumental; from then on his favor exceeded that of all other eunuchs, and Ma Zhi claimed to be related to him by clan.

sentences.zh: 上賜元贄寶帶，元贄以遺植，植服之以朝，上見而識之。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed on Yuanzan a jeweled belt; Yuanzan gave it to Ma Zhi, who wore it at court; the emperor saw it and recognized it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had bestowed a jeweled belt on Yuanzan; Yuanzan gave it to Ma Zhi, who wore it at court, and the emperor saw it and recognized it.

sentences.zh: 植變色，不敢隱。

translations.literal: Ma Zhi changed color and did not dare conceal the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhi turned pale and did not dare conceal it.

sentences.zh: 明日。

translations.literal: The next day,
translations.idiomatic: The next day,

sentences.zh: 罷相，收植親吏董侔，下御史台鞫之，盡得植與元贄交通之狀，再貶常州刺史。

translations.literal: he was removed as chief minister; Ma Zhi's personal clerk Dong Mou was seized and sent down to the Censorate for interrogation; the full circumstances of Ma Zhi's dealings with Yuanzan were obtained, and he was demoted again to prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: he was removed as chief minister; Ma Zhi's personal clerk Dong Mou was seized and interrogated at the Censorate; the full record of Ma Zhi's dealings with Yuanzan was obtained, and he was demoted again to prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊申，兵部侍郎、同平章事魏扶薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wushen, Vice Minister of War and Co-Equal Chief Minister Wei Fu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wushen, Vice Minister of War and Co-Equal Chief Minister Wei Fu died.

sentences.zh: 以戶部尚書、判度支崔龜從同平章事。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue and acting commissioner of fiscal affairs Cui Guicong was made Co-Equal Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue and acting commissioner of fiscal affairs Cui Guicong was made Co-Equal Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，以白敏中判延資庫。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Bai Minzhong was made acting director of the Yanzhi Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, Bai Minzhong was made acting director of the Yanzhi Treasury.

sentences.zh: 盧龍節度使周綝薨，軍中表請以押牙兼馬步都知兵馬使張允伸為留後。

translations.literal: Military commissioner of Lulong Zhou Zong died; the army submitted a memorial requesting that adjutant and concurrent commander of horse and foot forces Zhang Yunshen be made acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Military commissioner of Lulong Zhou Zong died; the army submitted a memorial requesting that adjutant and concurrent commander of horse and foot forces Zhang Yunshen be made acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁酉，從之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dingyou, the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingyou, the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 党項為邊患，發諸道兵討之，連年無功，戍饋不已，右補闕孔溫裕上疏切諫。

translations.literal: The Tangut people were a border menace; troops from various circuits were sent to attack them; for years there was no success, and frontier supplies were unceasing; Right Supplementation Censor Kong Wényù submitted a memorial strongly remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut were a border menace; troops from various circuits were sent against them; for years there was no success, and frontier supplies never ceased; Right Supplementation Censor Kong Wényù submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 上怒，貶柳州司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted him to defender of Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and demoted him to defender of Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 溫裕，戣之兄子也。

translations.literal: Wényù was the son of Kong Zhi's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wényù was a nephew of Kong Zhi.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃論恐熱遣僧莽羅藺真將兵於雞項關南造橋，以擊尚婢婢，軍於白土嶺。

translations.literal: The Tibetan Lun Qinlé sent the monk Mangluó Lánzhēn to lead troops to build a bridge south of Jixiang Pass to attack Shang Pipi; the army encamped at Baitu Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan Lun Qinlé sent the monk Mangluó Lánzhēn to lead troops to build a bridge south of Jixiang Pass to attack Shang Pipi; his army encamped at Baitu Ridge.

sentences.zh: 婢婢遣其將尚鐸羅榻藏將兵據臨蕃軍以拒之，不利，復遣磨離羆子、燭盧鞏力將兵據氂牛峽以拒之。

translations.literal: Pipi sent her general Shang Duóluó Tàzàng with troops to hold Linfan Army to resist him; this was unsuccessful, and she again sent Molí Pízi and Zhúlú Gǒnglì with troops to hold Maoniu Gorge to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Pipi sent her general Shang Duóluó Tàzàng with troops to hold Linfan Army against him; this failed, and she again sent Molí Pízi and Zhúlú Gǒnglì with troops to hold Maoniu Gorge against him.

sentences.zh: 鞏力請「按兵拒險，勿與戰，以奇兵絕其糧道，使進不得戰，退不得還，不過旬月，其眾必潰。」

translations.literal: Gǒnglì urged, "Hold the army in place and defend the defiles; do not give battle; use surprise troops to cut off their supply route, so that they can neither advance to fight nor retreat to return; within no more than ten days their host will surely disperse."
translations.idiomatic: Gǒnglì urged, "Hold the army in place and defend the defiles; do not give battle; use surprise troops to cut their supply line, so that they can neither advance to fight nor retreat to return; within no more than ten days their host will surely disperse."

sentences.zh: 羆子不從。

translations.literal: Pízi did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Pízi did not follow this advice.

sentences.zh: 鞏力曰：「吾寧為不用之人，不為敗軍之將。」

translations.literal: Gǒnglì said, "I would rather be a man unused than a general of a defeated army."
translations.idiomatic: Gǒnglì said, "I would rather be a man set aside than a general of a defeated army."

sentences.zh: 稱疾，歸鄯州。

translations.literal: He claimed illness and returned to Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed illness and returned to Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 羆子逆戰，敗死。

translations.literal: Pízi met the enemy in battle and was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Pízi met the enemy in battle, was defeated, and died.

sentences.zh: 婢婢糧乏，留拓跋懷光守鄯州，帥部落三千餘人就水草於甘州西。

translations.literal: Pipi was short of grain; she left Tuoba Huáiguāng to guard Shazhou and led more than three thousand tribesmen west of Ganzhou in search of pasture and water.
translations.idiomatic: Pipi lacked grain; she left Tuoba Huáiguāng to guard Shazhou and led more than three thousand of her tribesmen west of Ganzhou in search of pasture and water.

sentences.zh: 恐熱聞婢婢棄鄯州，自將輕騎五千追之。

translations.literal: When Qinlé heard that Pipi had abandoned Shazhou, he himself led five thousand light cavalry in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinlé heard that Pipi had abandoned Shazhou, he personally led five thousand light horsemen in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 至瓜州，聞懷光守鄯州，遂大掠河西鄯、廓等八州，殺其丁壯，劓刖其羸老及婦人，以槊貫嬰兒為戲，焚其室廬，五千里間，赤地殆盡。

translations.literal: Reaching Guazhou, he heard that Huáiguāng was holding Shazhou; he then plundered on a vast scale the eight prefectures of Hexi—Shazhou, Kuozhou, and the rest—killing their able-bodied men, cutting off the noses and ears of the weak elderly and women, spearing infants for sport, burning their dwellings; for five thousand li the land was nearly bare.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Guazhou, he heard that Huáiguāng held Shazhou; he then plundered on a vast scale the eight Hexi prefectures including Shazhou and Kuozhou—killing the able-bodied, cutting off the noses and ears of the weak elderly and women, spearing infants for sport, burning dwellings; for five thousand li the land was nearly bare.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛未，以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎令狐綯同平章事。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinwei, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War Linghu Tao was made Co-Equal Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinwei, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War Linghu Tao was made Co-Equal Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬寅，以翰林學士劉瑑為京西招討党項行營宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on renyin, Hanlin Academician Liu Zhuan was made commissioner for pacification of the western capital campaign to suppress the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renyin, Hanlin Academician Liu Zhuan was made commissioner for pacification of the western capital campaign to suppress the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 以盧龍留後張允伸為節度使。

translations.literal: Acting commissioner of Lulong Zhang Yunshen was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Acting commissioner of Lulong Zhang Yunshen was made military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以鳳翔節度使李業、河東節度使李試著兼招討党項使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, military commissioner of Fengxiang Li Ye and military commissioner of Hedong Li Shizhe were additionally made commissioners to suppress the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, military commissioner of Fengxiang Li Ye and military commissioner of Hedong Li Shizhe were additionally made commissioners to suppress the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎孔溫業白執政求外官，白敏中謂同列曰：「我輩須自點檢，孔吏部不肯居朝廷矣。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Kong Wényè informed the chief ministers that he sought an outside post; Bai Minzhong said to his colleagues, "We must examine ourselves: Vice Minister Kong no longer wishes to remain at court."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Kong Wényè informed the chief ministers that he sought an outside post; Bai Minzhong said to his colleagues, "We must examine ourselves—Vice Minister Kong no longer wishes to remain at court."

sentences.zh: 溫業，戣之弟子也。

translations.literal: Wényè was a disciple of Kong Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wényè was a disciple of Kong Zhi.

sentences.zh: 宣宗元聖至明成武獻文睿智章仁神聰懿道大孝皇帝下大中五年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuānzong (posthumous titles)—the latter part of his reign; fifth year of the Dazhong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuānzong (posthumous titles)—the latter part of his reign; fifth year of the Dazhong era (

sentences.zh: 辛未，公元八五一年）

translations.literal: xinwei, corresponding to 851 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinwei, 851 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，壬戌，天德軍奏攝沙州刺史張義潮遣使來降。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on renxu, the Tiande Army reported that acting prefect of Shazhou Zhang Yichao had sent envoys to submit and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on renxu, the Tiande Army reported that acting prefect of Shazhou Zhang Yichao had sent envoys to submit and surrender.

sentences.zh: 義潮，沙州人也，時吐蕃大亂，義潮陰結豪傑，謀自拔歸唐。

translations.literal: Yichao was a native of Shazhou; at the time Tibet was in great turmoil; Yichao secretly rallied the bold and planned to break free and return to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Yichao was a native of Shazhou; at the time Tibet was in great turmoil; Yichao secretly rallied bold men and planned to break free and return to Tang.

sentences.zh: 一旦，帥眾被甲噪於州門，唐人皆應之，吐番守將驚走，義潮遂攝州事，奉表來降。

translations.literal: One day he led his followers, armored, to clamor at the prefectural gate; all Tang people responded; the Tibetan garrison commander fled in alarm; Yichao then took charge of the prefecture and sent a memorial submitting to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: One day he led his followers, armored, to clamor at the prefectural gate; Tang people everywhere responded; the Tibetan garrison commander fled in alarm; Yichao then took charge of the prefecture and sent a memorial submitting to Tang.

sentences.zh: 以義潮為沙州防禦使。

translations.literal: Yichao was made defender of Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yichao was made defender of Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎裴休為鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Pei Xiu was made salt and iron transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Pei Xiu was made salt and iron transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 休，肅之子也。

translations.literal: Xiu was a son of Pei Su.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was a son of Pei Su.

sentences.zh: 自太和以來，歲運江、淮米不過四十萬斛，吏卒侵盜、沉沒，舟達渭倉者什不三四，大墮劉晏之法。

translations.literal: Since the Taihe era, the annual transport of rice from the Jianghuai region had not exceeded four hundred thousand hu; clerks and soldiers pilfered and sank it; of the boats that reached the Wei granary, not more than three or four in ten; Liu Yan's methods had greatly fallen away.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Taihe era, annual transport of Jianghuai rice had not exceeded four hundred thousand hu; clerks and soldiers pilfered and sank shipments; of boats reaching the Wei granary, scarcely three or four in ten; Liu Yan's methods had greatly decayed.

sentences.zh: 休窮究其弊，立漕法十條，歲運米至渭倉者百二十萬斛。

translations.literal: Xiu thoroughly investigated the abuses, established ten articles of transport law, and the annual rice reaching the Wei granary came to one million two hundred thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu thoroughly investigated the abuses, established ten articles of transport law, and annual rice reaching the Wei granary came to one million two hundred thousand hu.

sentences.zh: 上頗知党項之反由邊帥利其羊馬，數欺奪之，或妄誅殺，党項不勝憤怨，故反。

translations.literal: The emperor was well aware that the Tangut rebellion arose because frontier commanders coveted their sheep and horses, repeatedly cheated and seized them, or killed without cause; the Tangut could not bear their rage and resentment and therefore rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was well aware that the Tangut rebellion arose because frontier commanders coveted their sheep and horses, repeatedly cheated and seized them, or killed without cause; the Tangut could not bear their rage and resentment and therefore rebelled.

sentences.zh: 乃以右諫議大夫李福為夏綏節度使。

translations.literal: He therefore appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee Li Fu military commissioner of Xia-Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee Li Fu military commissioner of Xia-Sui.

sentences.zh: 自是繼選儒臣以代邊帥之貪暴者，行日復面加戒勵，党項由是遂安。

translations.literal: From this time civil officials were successively chosen to replace the greedy and violent frontier commanders; on the day of their departure the emperor again admonished them face to face; the Tangut were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: From this time civil officials were successively chosen to replace greedy and violent frontier commanders; on the day of departure the emperor again admonished them face to face; the Tangut were thereby pacified.

sentences.zh: 福，石之弟也。

translations.literal: Fu was a younger brother of Li Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was a younger brother of Li Shi.

sentences.zh: 上以南山、平夏党項久未平，頗厭用兵。

translations.literal: Because the Southern Mountain and Pingxia Tangut had long gone unpacified, the emperor was quite weary of using troops.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Southern Mountain and Pingxia Tangut had long gone unpacified, the emperor was quite weary of military campaigns.

sentences.zh: 崔鉉建議，宜遣大臣鎮撫。

translations.literal: Cui Xuan proposed that a senior minister should be sent to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan proposed that a senior minister should be sent to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 三月，以白敏中為司空、同平章事，充招討党項行營都統、制置等使，南北兩路供軍使兼邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month, Bai Minzhong was made Minister of Works and Co-Equal Chief Minister, and appointed overall commander of the campaign to suppress the Tangut, commissioner for disposition, commissioner for supplies on the northern and southern routes, and military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Bai Minzhong was made Minister of Works and Co-Equal Chief Minister, overall commander of the campaign to suppress the Tangut, commissioner for disposition, commissioner for supplies on the northern and southern routes, and military commissioner of Binning.

sentences.zh: 敏中請用裴度故事，擇廷臣為將佐，許之。

translations.literal: Minzhong requested to follow Pei Du's precedent and choose court officials as staff; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong requested to follow Pei Du's precedent and choose court officials as staff; this was granted.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，以左諫議大夫孫景商為左庶子，充邠寧行軍司馬；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Left Remonstrance Grandee Sun Jingshang was made Left Household Mentor and campaign marshal of Binning;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Left Remonstrance Grandee Sun Jingshang was made Left Household Mentor and campaign marshal of Binning;

sentences.zh: 知制誥蔣伸為右庶子，充節度副使。

translations.literal: Drafter of Proclamations Jiang Shen was made Right Household Mentor and deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Drafter of Proclamations Jiang Shen was made Right Household Mentor and deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 伸，系之弟也。

translations.literal: Shen was a younger brother of Jiang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was a younger brother of Jiang Xi.

sentences.zh: 初，上令白敏中為萬壽公主選佳婿，敏中薦鄭顥。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had ordered Bai Minzhong to select a fine son-in-law for Princess Wanshou; Minzhong recommended Zheng Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor had ordered Bai Minzhong to select a fine son-in-law for Princess Wanshou; Minzhong recommended Zheng Hao.

sentences.zh: 時顥已昏盧氏，行至鄭州，堂帖追還，顥甚銜之，由是數毀敏中於上。

translations.literal: At the time Hao had already married the Lu clan; when he reached Zhengzhou, an urgent palace dispatch recalled him; Hao deeply resented this and thereafter repeatedly slandered Minzhong to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hao had already married into the Lu clan; when he reached Zhengzhou, an urgent palace dispatch recalled him; Hao deeply resented this and thereafter repeatedly slandered Minzhong to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 敏中將赴鎮，言於上曰：「鄭顥不樂尚主，怨臣入骨髓。

translations.literal: As Minzhong was about to depart for his command, he said to the emperor, "Zheng Hao did not wish to marry the princess; his hatred of me goes to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: As Minzhong was about to depart for his command, he said to the emperor, "Zheng Hao did not wish to marry the princess; his hatred of me goes to the marrow.

sentences.zh: 臣在政府，無如臣何；

translations.literal: While I am in the government, he can do nothing to me;
translations.idiomatic: While I remain in the government, he can do nothing to me;

sentences.zh: 今臣出外，顥必中傷，臣死無日矣！」

translations.literal: now that I go outside, Hao will surely strike at me—I have not long to live!"
translations.idiomatic: now that I go outside, Hao will surely strike at me—I have not long to live!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕知之久矣，卿何言之晚邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I have known this for a long time—why do you speak of it only now!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have known this for a long time—why do you speak of it only now!"

sentences.zh: 命左右於禁中取小檉函以授敏中曰：「此皆鄭郎譖卿之書也。

translations.literal: He ordered attendants to take from the inner quarters a small catalpa box and give it to Minzhong, saying, "These are all Master Zheng's letters slandering you.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered attendants to take from the inner quarters a small catalpa box and give it to Minzhong, saying, "These are all Master Zheng's letters slandering you.

sentences.zh: 朕若信之，豈任卿以至今日！」

translations.literal: Had I believed them, how could I have entrusted you with office until today!"
translations.idiomatic: Had I believed them, how could I have entrusted you with office until today!"

sentences.zh: 敏中歸，置檉函於佛前，焚香事之。

translations.literal: Minzhong returned home, placed the catalpa box before the Buddha, and burned incense before it.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong returned home, placed the catalpa box before the Buddha, and burned incense before it.

sentences.zh: 敏中軍於寧州，壬子，定遠城使史元破堂項九千餘帳於三交谷，敏中奏党項平。

translations.literal: Minzhong encamped at Ningzhou; on renzi, Defender of Dingyuan City Shi Yuan broke more than nine thousand Tangut tents of the Tang clan at Sanjiao Valley; Minzhong memorialized that the Tangut were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong encamped at Ningzhou; on renzi, Defender of Dingyuan City Shi Yuan broke more than nine thousand Tangut tents of the Tang clan at Sanjiao Valley; Minzhong memorialized that the Tangut were pacified.

sentences.zh: 辛未，詔：「平夏党項，已就安貼。

translations.literal: On xinwei, an edict stated: "The Pingxia Tangut have already been settled.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, an edict stated: "The Pingxia Tangut have already been settled.

sentences.zh: 南山党項，聞出山者迫於饑寒，猶行鈔掠，平夏不容，窮無所歸。

translations.literal: The Southern Mountain Tangut, hearing that those who came out of the mountains were driven by hunger and cold, still carried out raids; Pingxia would not receive them, and they had nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Mountain Tangut, hearing that those who came out of the mountains were driven by hunger and cold, still carried out raids; Pingxia would not receive them, and they had nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 宜委李福存諭，於銀、夏境內授以閒田。

translations.literal: Li Fu should be entrusted to go and instruct them and grant them idle land within the Yin and Xia borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu should be entrusted to go and instruct them and grant them idle land within the Yin and Xia borderlands.

sentences.zh: 如能革心向化，則撫如赤子，從前為惡，一切不問，或有抑屈，聽於本鎮投牒自訴。

translations.literal: If they reform their hearts and turn to civilization, treat them as infants; for past wrongdoing, ask nothing; if there is oppression, let them submit petitions of grievance to their own circuit.
translations.idiomatic: If they reform their hearts and turn to civilization, treat them as infants; for past wrongdoing, ask nothing; if there is oppression, let them submit petitions of grievance to their own circuit.

sentences.zh: 若再犯疆場，或復入山林，不受教令，則誅討無赦。

translations.literal: If they again violate the borderlands or return to the mountains and refuse instruction, then execute and punish without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: If they again violate the borderlands or return to the mountains and refuse instruction, then execute and punish without pardon.

sentences.zh: 將吏有功者甄獎，死傷者優恤。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers with merit shall be selected and rewarded; the dead and wounded shall receive generous relief.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers with merit shall be selected and rewarded; the dead and wounded shall receive generous relief.

sentences.zh: 靈、夏、邠、鄜四道百姓，給復三年，鄰道量免租稅。

translations.literal: The people of the four circuits Ling, Xia, Bin, and Fu shall receive tax relief for three years; neighboring circuits shall have rents and taxes reduced as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the four circuits Ling, Xia, Bin, and Fu shall receive tax relief for three years; neighboring circuits shall have rents and taxes reduced as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 向由邊將貪鄙，致其怨叛，自今當更擇廉良撫之。

translations.literal: Formerly frontier generals' greed and baseness caused their resentment and rebellion; from now on more honest and good men must be chosen to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly frontier generals' greed and baseness caused their resentment and rebellion; from now on more honest and good men must be chosen to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 若復致侵叛，當先罪邊將，後討寇虜。」

translations.literal: If invasion and rebellion occur again, the frontier generals shall be punished first, and only afterward shall the marauders be attacked."
translations.idiomatic: If invasion and rebellion occur again, the frontier generals shall be punished first, and only afterward shall the marauders be attacked."

sentences.zh: 吐蕃論恐熱殘虐，所部多叛。

translations.literal: The Tibetan Lun Qinlé was cruel and tyrannical; many of his followers rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan Lun Qinlé was cruel and tyrannical; many of his followers rebelled.

sentences.zh: 拓跋懷光使人說誘之，其眾或散歸部落，或降於懷光。

translations.literal: Tuoba Huáiguāng sent men to persuade and entice them; some dispersed to their tribes, some surrendered to Huáiguāng.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Huáiguāng sent men to persuade and entice them; some dispersed to their tribes, some surrendered to Huáiguāng.

sentences.zh: 恐熱勢孤，乃揚言於眾曰：「吾今入朝於唐，借兵五十萬來誅不服者，然後以渭州為國城，請唐冊我為贊普，誰敢不從！」

translations.literal: Qinlé, isolated in power, then proclaimed to the host, "I shall now enter Tang and borrow five hundred thousand troops to execute those who will not submit; then I shall take Weizhou as my capital and ask Tang to invest me as zanpu—who will not follow!"
translations.idiomatic: Qinlé, isolated in power, then proclaimed to the host, "I shall now enter Tang and borrow five hundred thousand troops to execute those who will not submit; then I shall take Weizhou as my capital and ask Tang to invest me as zanpu—who will not follow!"

sentences.zh: 五月，恐熱入朝，上遣左丞李景讓就禮賓院問所欲。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Qinlé entered court; the emperor sent Left Vice Director Li Jingrang to the Office of Guests to inquire what he desired.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Qinlé entered court; the emperor sent Left Vice Director Li Jingrang to the Office of Guests to inquire what he desired.

sentences.zh: 恐熱氣色驕倨，語言荒誕，求為河渭節度使。

translations.literal: Qinlé's bearing was arrogant and haughty; his words were wild and absurd; he sought to be military commissioner of the He and Wei region.
translations.idiomatic: Qinlé's bearing was arrogant and haughty; his words were wild and absurd; he sought to be military commissioner of the He and Wei region.

sentences.zh: 上不許，召對三殿，如常日胡客，勞賜遣還。

translations.literal: The emperor did not grant this; he was summoned to audience in the Three Halls as on ordinary days for barbarian guests, rewarded, and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not grant this; he was summoned to audience in the Three Halls as on ordinary days for barbarian guests, rewarded, and sent back.

sentences.zh: 恐熱怏怏而去，復歸落門川，聚其舊眾，欲為邊患。

translations.literal: Qinlé departed resentfully; he returned to Luomen River, gathered his old followers, and intended to become a border menace.
translations.idiomatic: Qinlé departed resentfully; he returned to Luomen River, gathered his old followers, and intended to become a border menace.

sentences.zh: 會久雨，乏食，眾稍散，才有三百餘人，奔於廓州。

translations.literal: As prolonged rain left them short of food, the host gradually dispersed; he had only a little more than three hundred men and fled to Kuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: As prolonged rain left them short of food, the host gradually dispersed; he had only a little more than three hundred men and fled to Kuozhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，立皇子潤為鄂王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the emperor's son Run was established as Prince of E.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the emperor's son Run was established as Prince of E.

sentences.zh: 進士孫樵上言：「百姓男耕女織，不自溫飽，而群僧安坐華屋，美衣精饌，率以十戶不能養一僧。

translations.literal: Presented scholar Sun Qiao submitted a memorial stating, "The common people, men plowing and women weaving, cannot warm and feed themselves, while groups of monks sit at ease in splendid halls, in fine clothes and choice food—on average ten households cannot support one monk.
translations.idiomatic: Presented scholar Sun Qiao submitted a memorial stating, "The common people, men plowing and women weaving, cannot warm and feed themselves, while groups of monks sit at ease in splendid halls, in fine clothes and choice food—on average ten households cannot support one monk.

sentences.zh: 武宗憤其然，發十七萬僧，是天下一百七十萬戶始得蘇息也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong resented this and expelled one hundred seventy thousand monks; only then could one million seven hundred thousand households begin to breathe again.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong resented this and expelled one hundred seventy thousand monks; only then could one million seven hundred thousand households begin to breathe again.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位以來，修復廢寺，天下斧斤之聲至今不絕，度僧幾復其舊矣。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, ruined monasteries have been restored; the sound of axes throughout the realm has not ceased to this day; ordained monks have nearly returned to the former numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, ruined monasteries have been restored; the sound of axes throughout the realm has not ceased to this day; ordained monks have nearly returned to the former numbers.

sentences.zh: 陛下縱不能如武宗除積弊，奈何興之於已廢乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty, though unable to remove accumulated abuses as Wuzong did, how can you revive what has already been abolished!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, though unable to remove accumulated abuses as Wuzong did, how can you revive what has already been abolished!

sentences.zh: 日者陛下欲修國東門，諫官上言，遽為罷役。

translations.literal: Recently Your Majesty wished to repair the eastern gate of the capital; remonstrating officials submitted memorials, and the work was promptly halted.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Your Majesty wished to repair the eastern gate of the capital; remonstrating officials submitted memorials, and the work was promptly halted.

sentences.zh: 今所復之寺，豈若東門之急乎？

translations.literal: Are the monasteries now being restored not more urgent than the eastern gate?
translations.idiomatic: Are the monasteries now being restored not more urgent than the eastern gate?

sentences.zh: 所役之功，豈右東門之勞乎？

translations.literal: Is the labor expended not greater than that for the eastern gate?
translations.idiomatic: Is the labor expended not greater than that for the eastern gate?

sentences.zh: 願早降明詔，僧未復者勿復，寺未修者勿修，庶幾百姓猶得以息肩也。」

translations.literal: I pray that an enlightened edict be issued soon: where monks have not been restored, do not restore them; where monasteries have not been repaired, do not repair them—then perhaps the common people may yet rest their shoulders."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that an enlightened edict be issued soon: where monks have not been restored, do not restore them; where monasteries have not been repaired, do not repair them—then perhaps the common people may yet rest their shoulders."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，中書門下奏：「陛下崇奉釋氏，群下莫不奔走，恐財力有所不逮，因之生事擾人，望委所在長吏量加撙節。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized, "Your Majesty reveres the Buddha; below, none do not rush to follow; we fear finances may not suffice and thereby give rise to affairs that disturb the people; we hope the local chief officials may be entrusted to practice restraint as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized, "Your Majesty reveres the Buddha; below, none do not rush to follow; we fear finances may not suffice and thereby give rise to affairs that disturb the people; we hope the local chief officials may be entrusted to practice restraint as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 所度僧亦委選擇有行業者，若容凶粗之人，則更非敬道也。

translations.literal: Those ordained as monks should also be chosen from among men of conduct; if coarse and violent men are admitted, that is even less reverence for the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Those ordained as monks should also be chosen from among men of conduct; if coarse and violent men are admitted, that is even less reverence for the Way.

sentences.zh: 鄉村佛捨，請罷兵日修。」

translations.literal: Village Buddhist shrines—please halt military days for repairs."
translations.idiomatic: Village Buddhist shrines—please halt military days for repairs."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: This was followed.

sentences.zh: 八月，白敏中奏，南山党項亦請降。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Bai Minzhong memorialized that the Southern Mountain Tangut also requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Bai Minzhong reported that the Southern Mountain Tangut were also seeking to surrender.

sentences.zh: 時用兵歲久，國用頗乏，詔並赦南山党項，使之安業。

translations.literal: At the time troops had been employed for many years and state finances were quite strained; an edict granted a general amnesty to the Southern Mountain Tangut and allowed them to settle in peace.
translations.idiomatic: With the war having dragged on for years and state finances strained, the court proclaimed a general amnesty for the Southern Mountain Tangut so they could settle in peace.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙卯，中書門下奏：「今邊事已息，而州府諸寺尚未畢功，望且令成之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yimao, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "Now that border affairs have ceased, monasteries in prefectures and circuits are not yet finished; we hope they may be allowed to be completed for the present.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on yimao, the Secretariat and Chancellery submitted: "Border affairs have quieted, yet prefectural monasteries remain unfinished—we ask that they be allowed to reach completion for now.

sentences.zh: 其大縣遠於州府者，聽置一寺，其鄉村毋得更置佛捨。」

translations.literal: In large counties distant from the prefectural seat, one monastery may be established; in villages, Buddhist shrines must not be established anew."
translations.idiomatic: Large counties far from their prefectural seats might keep one monastery; villages must not add new Buddhist shrines."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以戶部侍郎魏謨同平章事，仍判戶部。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Vice Minister of Revenue Wei Mo was made Co-Equal Chief Minister and continued to act as minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Vice Minister of Revenue Wei Mo was made Co-Equal Chief Minister while retaining charge of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時上春秋已高，未立太子，群臣莫敢言。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was already advanced in years and had not yet established an heir apparent; none among the ministers dared speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was already advanced in years and had not named a crown prince; none of the ministers dared raise the matter.

sentences.zh: 謨入謝，因言：「今海內無事，惟未建儲副，使正人輔導，臣竊以為憂。」

translations.literal: When Mo entered to give thanks for appointment, he spoke further: "Now within the seas there is no trouble, yet the heir apparent has not been established and upright men have not been appointed to guide him—I venture to regard this with anxiety."
translations.idiomatic: At his audience of thanks, Mo added: "The realm is at peace, yet no heir apparent has been installed and no upright tutors appointed—I cannot help but worry."

sentences.zh: 且泣。

translations.literal: And he wept.
translations.idiomatic: He wept as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 時人重之。

translations.literal: People of the time esteemed him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries held him in high regard for this.

sentences.zh: 蓬、果群盜依阻雞山，寇掠三川。

translations.literal: Bandits of Peng and Guo relied on Jishan for refuge and raided the Three Rivers region.
translations.idiomatic: Brigands from Peng and Guo held Jishan and raided the Three Rivers region.

sentences.zh: 以果州刺史王贄弘充三川行營都知兵馬使，以討之。

translations.literal: Prefect of Guo Wang Zanhong was appointed overall commander of horse and infantry of the Three Rivers campaign headquarters to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zanhong, prefect of Guo, was made overall commander of the Three Rivers campaign to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 制以党項既平，罷白敏中教統，但以司空、平章事充邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: By decree, because the Tangut had been pacified, Bai Minzhong was removed as campaign commander-in-chief and made only Minister of Works, Co-Equal Chief Minister, and military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: An edict relieved Bai Minzhong of his campaign command—he remained Minister of Works, Co-Equal Chief Minister, and military commissioner of Binning.

sentences.zh: 張義潮發兵略定其旁瓜、伊、西、甘、肅、蘭、鄯、河、岷、廓十州，遣其兄義澤奉十一州圖籍入見，於是河、湟之地盡入於唐。

translations.literal: Zhang Yichao sent troops to seize by degrees the ten prefectures beside him—Gua, Yi, Xi, Gan, Su, Lan, Shan, He, Min, and Kuo—and sent his elder brother Yize to present maps and registers of the eleven prefectures at court; the lands of the He and Huang region thus all entered Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yichao dispatched troops to secure the ten neighboring prefectures—Gua, Yi, Xi, Gan, Su, Lan, Shan, He, Min, and Kuo—and sent his elder brother Yize to court with maps and registers of all eleven; the He-Huang region thus returned fully to Tang control.

sentences.zh: 十一月，置歸義軍於沙州，以義潮為節度使、十一州觀察使，又以義潮判官曹義金為歸義軍長史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Guiyi Army was established at Shazhou; Yichao was made its military commissioner and commissioner overseeing the eleven prefectures; Yichao's aide Cao Yijin was made chief secretary of the Guiyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the court founded the Guiyi Army at Shazhou, appointing Yichao military commissioner and overseer of the eleven prefectures, with his aide Cao Yijin as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 以中書侍郎、同平章事崔龜從同平章事，充宣武節度使。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal Chief Minister Cui Guicong was made Co-Equal Chief Minister and military commissioner of Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Guicong was transferred to military commissioner of Xuanwu while retaining his chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 右羽林統軍張直方坐出獵累日不還宿衛，貶左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Commander of the Right Forest Army Zhang Zhifang, for going hunting several days without returning to palace guard duty, was demoted to general of the Left Xiaowei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhifang, commander of the Right Forest Army, was demoted to general of the Left Xiaowei for hunting several days without returning to guard duty.

sentences.zh: 宣宗元聖至明成武獻文睿智章仁神聰懿道大孝皇帝下大中六年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuānzong (posthumous titles)—the latter part of his reign; sixth year of the Dazhong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuānzong (posthumous titles)—the latter part of his reign; sixth year of the Dazhong era (

sentences.zh: 壬申，公元八五二年）

translations.literal: renshen, corresponding to 852 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renshen, 852 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，王贄弘討雞山賊，平之。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, Wang Zanhong attacked the Jishan bandits and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, Wang Zanhong defeated the Jishan bandits and restored order.

sentences.zh: 是時，山南西道節度使封敖奏巴南妖賊言辭悖慢，上怒甚。

translations.literal: At this time military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit Feng Ao memorialized that demonic rebels south of Ba spoke with insolent and disrespectful words; the emperor was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ao, military commissioner of Shannan West, reported that rebel bands south of Ba used defiant language; the emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 崔鉉曰：「此皆陛下赤子，迫於饑寒，盜弄陛下兵於溪谷間，不足辱大軍，但遣一使者可平矣。」

translations.literal: Cui Xuan said, "These are all Your Majesty's children, driven by hunger and cold to wield Your Majesty's soldiers in ravines and valleys; they are not worth troubling a great army—a single envoy can pacify them."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan said, "They are Your Majesty's own people, starving into banditry in the hills; a great army is unnecessary—one envoy should suffice."

sentences.zh: 乃遣京兆少尹劉潼詣果州招諭之。

translations.literal: The court therefore sent Junior Vice Prefect of the Capital Liu Tong to Guo Prefecture to summon and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Liu Tong, junior vice prefect of the capital, to Guo Prefecture to offer terms.

sentences.zh: 潼上言請不發兵攻討，且曰：「今以日月之明燭愚迷之眾，使之稽顙歸命，其勢甚易。

translations.literal: Tong memorialized requesting that troops not be sent to attack, and said further, "Now with the brightness of sun and moon to illuminate this foolish and benighted host, making them bow their foreheads and submit is very easy in its tendency.
translations.idiomatic: Tong asked that no attack be launched, writing: "With the court's authority shining on them, they will kneel and submit—the matter should be easy.

sentences.zh: 所慮者，武臣恥不戰之功，議者責欲速之效耳。」

translations.literal: What is feared is that military men will be ashamed of gaining no battle merit and councillors will blame us for seeking too slow an effect."
translations.idiomatic: My concern is only that generals hunger for battle-glory and officials demand quick results."

sentences.zh: 潼至山中，盜彎弓待之，潼屏左右直前曰：「我面受詔赦汝罪，使汝復為平人。

translations.literal: Tong reached the mountains; the bandits strung bows to await him; Tong dismissed his attendants and went forward directly, saying, "I have received an edict face to face to pardon your crimes and restore you as peaceful people.
translations.idiomatic: In the hills the bandits drew their bows; Tong sent away his escort and stepped forward: "I carry an edict pardoning you and restoring you as ordinary subjects.

sentences.zh: 聞汝木弓射二百步，今我去汝十步，汝真欲反者，可射我！」

translations.literal: I have heard your wooden bows shoot two hundred paces; now I stand ten paces from you—if you truly wish to rebel, you may shoot me!"
translations.idiomatic: Your bows are said to carry two hundred paces; I stand ten paces away—if you mean to fight, shoot me now!"

sentences.zh: 賊皆投弓列拜，請降。

translations.literal: The bandits all cast down their bows, formed ranks, and bowed, requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They dropped their bows, lined up, and begged to surrender.

sentences.zh: 潼歸館，而王贄弘與中使似先義逸引兵已至山下，竟擊滅之。

translations.literal: Tong returned to his lodging, but Wang Zanhong and the palace envoy Si Xianyi had already led troops to the foot of the mountain and in the end attacked and destroyed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Tong returned to quarters—but Wang Zanhong and the palace envoy Si Xianyi were already at the mountain foot and annihilated the bandits.

sentences.zh: 三月，敕先賜右衛大將軍鄭光鄠縣及雲陽莊並免稅役。

translations.literal: In the third month, an edict granted in advance to General of the Right Guard Zheng Guang the estates of E County and Yunyang, together with exemption from taxes and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month an edict preemptively granted General Zheng Guang estates in E and Yunyang counties, exempt from tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 中書門下奏，以為：「稅役之法，天下皆同。

translations.literal: The Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized, holding that, "The law of taxes and corvée is the same throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat and Chancellery objected: "Tax and corvée law must be uniform empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 陛下屢發德音，欲使中外畫一，今獨免鄭光，似稍乖前意。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has repeatedly issued gracious edicts wishing to make inner and outer uniform; now to exempt Zheng Guang alone seems slightly at odds with your former intent.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has often proclaimed uniformity between court and provinces; exempting Zheng Guang alone seems at odds with that aim.

sentences.zh: 事雖至細，系體則多。」

translations.literal: Though the matter is extremely minute, what it touches in principle is great."
translations.idiomatic: The matter is small, but the principle is large."

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「朕以鄭光元舅之尊貴，欲優異令免徵稅，初不細思。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "I, considering Zheng Guang's eminence as maternal uncle, wished to favor him exceptionally by exempting him from levies—I did not think it through at first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "I meant to favor my uncle Zheng Guang and exempted his levies without thinking it through.

sentences.zh: 況親戚之間，人所難議，卿等苟非愛我，豈進嘉言！

translations.literal: Moreover, among kin, what men find hard to discuss—if you were not those who love me, how would you offer such excellent words!
translations.idiomatic: Among kin, criticism is hardest—had you not loved me, you would not have spoken so well!

sentences.zh: 庶事能盡如斯，天下何憂不理！

translations.literal: If all affairs can be carried through like this, what worry is there that the realm will not be well governed!
translations.idiomatic: If every matter were handled thus, how could the realm fail to prosper!

sentences.zh: 有始有卒，當共守之，並依所奏。」

translations.literal: From beginning to end we must jointly uphold this; all shall follow your memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Let us uphold this from start to finish and follow your memorial."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲辰，以邠寧節度使白敏中為西川節度使。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiachen, military commissioner of Binning Bai Minzhong was made military commissioner of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiachen, Bai Minzhong was transferred from Binning to military commissioner of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 湖南奏，團練副使馮少端討衡州賊帥鄧裴，平之。

translations.literal: Hunan reported that training commissioner deputy Feng Shaoduan attacked the bandit chieftain Deng Pei of Hengzhou and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan reported that Feng Shaoduan, deputy training commissioner, had suppressed Deng Pei, bandit leader of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 党項復擾邊，上欲擇可為邠寧帥者而難其人，從容與翰林學士、中書舍人須昌畢諴論邊事，諴援古據今，具陳方略。

translations.literal: The Tangut again disturbed the border; the emperor wished to choose someone who could be military commissioner of Binning but found the man hard to select; he spoke at leisure with Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafter Bi Xie of Xuchang about border affairs, and Xie cited antiquity and the present, setting forth strategy in full.
translations.idiomatic: Tangut raids resumed; the emperor sought a new Binning commander but found no obvious choice. Chatting with Hanlin drafter Bi Xie, he heard a full strategic brief drawing on past and present.

sentences.zh: 上悅曰：「吾方擇帥，不意頗、牧近在禁廷。

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure, "I am just now choosing a commander—I did not expect that Li and Mu are near at hand in the forbidden court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said gladly, "I am choosing a commander—and find my Li Mu right here in the palace.

sentences.zh: 卿其為朕行乎！」

translations.literal: Will you go on my behalf!"
translations.idiomatic: Will you go for me!"

sentences.zh: 諴欣然奉命。

translations.literal: Xie gladly accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Xie accepted with alacrity.

sentences.zh: 上欲重其資履，六月，壬申，先以諴為刑部侍郎，癸酉，乃除邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to weight his credentials; in the sixth month, on renshen, Xie was first made vice minister of justice; on guiyou he was appointed military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: To dignify his appointment, in the sixth month Xie was first made vice minister of justice on renshen, then military commissioner of Binning on guiyou.

sentences.zh: 雍王水美薨，追謚靖懷太子。

translations.literal: Prince Yong, Shuimei, died; he was posthumously titled Crown Prince Jinghuai.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong Shuimei died and was posthumously titled Crown Prince Jinghuai.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使李業縱吏民侵掠雜虜，又妄殺降者，由是北邊擾動。

translations.literal: Military commissioner of Hedong Li Ye allowed clerks and people to plunder and encroach on various barbarians, and also killed surrendered men without cause; the northern border was thereby disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye of Hedong let his staff and people prey on frontier tribes and killed surrendering tribesmen without cause, unsettling the north.

sentences.zh: 閏月，庚子，以太子少師盧鈞為河東節度使。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on gengzi, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent Lu Jun was made military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on gengzi, Lu Jun, junior tutor to the heir apparent, replaced him as military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 業內有所恃，人莫敢言，魏謨獨請貶黜。

translations.literal: Ye had backing within the palace; none dared speak against him; only Wei Mo requested his demotion and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Ye enjoyed palace backing and went unchallenged until Wei Mo alone demanded his removal.

sentences.zh: 上不許，但徙義成節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent but only transferred him to military commissioner of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused removal and merely transferred him to military commissioner of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 盧鈞奏度支郎中韋宙為副使。

translations.literal: Lu Jun memorialized recommending Wei Zhou, director in the Ministry of Revenue, as deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jun recommended Wei Zhou of the Ministry of Revenue as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 宙遍詣塞下，悉召酋長，諭以禍福，禁唐民毋得入虜境侵掠，犯者必死，雜虜由是遂安。

translations.literal: Zhou went everywhere below the passes, summoned all chieftains, instructed them on fortune and misfortune, forbade Tang people to enter barbarian territory to plunder—violators would die—and the various barbarians were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou toured the frontier, summoned every chieftain, warned them of consequences, and forbade Tang subjects to raid tribal lands on pain of death; the tribes quieted.

sentences.zh: 掌書記李璋杖一牙職，明日，牙將百餘人訴於鈞，鈞杖其為首者，摘戍外鎮，餘皆罰之，曰：「邊鎮百餘人，無故橫訴，不可不抑。」

translations.literal: Recorder Li Zhang beat a yamen clerk; the next day more than a hundred military officers appealed to Jun; Jun beat the ringleader, selected him for garrison duty in an outer fort, and punished the rest, saying, "On the frontier, more than a hundred men lodge groundless appeals—they cannot go unchecked."
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Li Zhang flogged a clerk; next day a hundred officers petitioned Jun, who flogged the leader, posted him to an outer fort, and punished the rest: "A hundred men cannot bully the command with false grievances."

sentences.zh: 璋，絳之子也。

translations.literal: Zhang was a son of Li Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was Li Jiang's son.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲子，以禮部尚書裴休同平章事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiazi, Minister of Rites Pei Xiu was made Co-Equal Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiazi, Minister of Rites Pei Xiu joined the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 獠寇昌、資二州。

translations.literal: Liao raided Chang and Zi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Liao tribes raided Chang and Zi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，邠寧節度使畢諴奏招諭党項皆降。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, military commissioner of Binning Bi Xie memorialized that through summons and instruction all Tangut had surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Bi Xie reported that all Tangut groups had submitted after his summons.

sentences.zh: 驍衛將軍張直方坐以小過屢殺奴婢，貶恩州司戶。

translations.literal: General of the Xiaowei Zhang Zhifang, for repeatedly killing slave girls over trifles, was demoted to registrar of En Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhifang of the Xiaowei was demoted to registrar of En for killing servant girls over petty offenses.

sentences.zh: 十一月，立憲宗子惴為棣王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the emperor's son Zhui, son of Emperor Xianzong, was established as Prince of Di.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor enfeoffed Zhui, a son of Emperor Xianzong, as Prince of Di.

sentences.zh: 十二月，中書門下奏：「度僧不精，則戒法墮壞；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "If ordained monks are not select, the precepts and law will fall into ruin;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Secretariat and Chancellery warned: "Careless ordination corrupts monastic discipline;

sentences.zh: 造寺無節，則損費過多，請自今諸州准元敕許置寺外，有勝地靈跡許修復，繁會之縣許置一院。

translations.literal: if monasteries are built without restraint, expense will be excessive; we request that hereafter, apart from monasteries permitted by the Yuan edict in each prefecture, where there are famous sites and numinous traces repair may be allowed, and in populous counties one cloister may be established.
translations.idiomatic: unrestrained temple-building wastes revenue. Henceforth let each prefecture keep only Yuan-era authorized temples, allow repairs only at sacred sites, and limit populous counties to one cloister.

sentences.zh: 嚴禁私度僧、尼。

translations.literal: Private ordination of monks and nuns is strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Private ordinations of monks and nuns are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 若官度僧、尼有闕，則擇人補之，仍申祠部給牒。

translations.literal: If official quotas for monks and nuns fall short, persons shall be chosen to fill them, and memorials submitted to the Ministry of Rites for certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Where official quotas lack monks or nuns, appoint qualified persons and obtain certificates from the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 其欲遠遊尋師者，須有本州公驗。」

translations.literal: Those who wish to travel far to seek teachers must have certification from their home prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Monks seeking distant teachers must carry home-prefecture credentials."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations were adopted.

sentences.zh: 宣宗元聖至明成武獻文睿智章仁神聰懿道大孝皇帝下大中七年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuānzong (posthumous titles)—the latter part of his reign; seventh year of the Dazhong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuānzong (posthumous titles)—the latter part of his reign; seventh year of the Dazhong era (

sentences.zh: 癸酉，公元八五三年）

translations.literal: guiyou, corresponding to 853 CE)
translations.idiomatic: guiyou, 853 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊申，上祀圓丘；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on wushen, the emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on wushen, the emperor performed the suburban sacrifice at the Round Mound;

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: he then proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙寅，敕：「自今法司處罪，用常行杖。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingyin, an edict stated: "From now on, when the judicial offices impose punishment, the regular staff shall be used.
translations.idiomatic: “In summer, the fourth month, on bingyin, an edict standardized judicial beatings:

sentences.zh: 杖脊一，折法杖十；

translations.literal: One stroke on the back counts as ten blows of the regulation staff;
translations.idiomatic: one blow to the back would equal ten regulation-staff strokes;

sentences.zh: 杖臀一，折笞五。

translations.literal: one stroke on the buttocks counts as five blows of the light cane.
translations.idiomatic: one blow to the buttocks would equal five light-cane strokes.

sentences.zh: 使吏用法有常准。」

translations.literal: Thus clerks would have a fixed standard in applying the law."
translations.idiomatic: Clerks would thus apply punishments by a fixed rule."

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，左補闕趙璘請罷來年元會，止御宣政。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, Left Supplementation Censor Zhao Lin requested that next year's New Year assembly be halted and that the emperor attend only at Xuanzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, Zhao Lin asked to cancel the New Year grand audience and confine the emperor to Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 上以問宰相，對曰：「元會大禮，不可罷。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chief ministers; they replied, "The New Year assembly is a great ritual—it cannot be halted.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers answered: "The New Year rite is too important to cancel.

sentences.zh: 況天下無事。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the realm is without trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the empire is at peace."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「近華州奏有賊光火劫下邽，關中少雪，皆朕之憂，何謂無事！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Recently Hua Prefecture reported bandits raiding Xia Gui by torchlight, and in the Guanzhong region snow has been scant—all are my worries; how can you say there is no trouble!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor retorted: "Hua reports torch raids on Xia Gui, and Guanzhong lacks snow—how is that 'no trouble'?

sentences.zh: 雖宣政亦不可御也。」

translations.literal: Even Xuanzheng Hall cannot be attended."
translations.idiomatic: I will not attend even Xuanzheng."

sentences.zh: 上事鄭太后甚謹，不居別宮，朝夕奉養。

translations.literal: The emperor served Empress Dowager Zheng with great care, did not reside in a separate palace, and morning and evening attended and nourished her.
translations.idiomatic: He served Empress Dowager Zheng devotedly, never living apart, attending her morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 舅鄭光歷平盧、河中節度使。

translations.literal: His maternal uncle Zheng Guang had served as military commissioner of Pinglu and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal uncle Zheng Guang had governed Pinglu and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 入朝，上與之論為政，光應對鄙淺，上不悅，留為右羽林統軍，使奉朝請。

translations.literal: When he entered court, the emperor discussed governing with him; Guang's replies were coarse and shallow; the emperor was displeased, kept him as commander of the Right Forest Army, and had him attend court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor discussed policy with Guang, whose answers proved crude; displeased, he kept Guang as a ceremonial general of the Right Forest.

sentences.zh: 太后數言其貧，上輒厚賜金帛，終不復任以民宮。

translations.literal: The empress dowager repeatedly spoke of his poverty; the emperor would lavish gold and silk, but never again entrusted him with a civil post governing the people.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager often pleaded his poverty; the emperor gave gold and silk generously but never again gave him a civil governorship.

sentences.zh: 度支奏：「自河、湟平，每歲天下所納錢九百二十五萬餘緡，內五百五十萬餘緡租稅，八十二萬餘緡榷酤，二百七十八萬餘緡鹽利。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue memorialized: "Since the He and Huang region was pacified, each year the money submitted from throughout the realm came to more than nine million two hundred fifty thousand strings—of which more than five million five hundred thousand strings were rents and taxes, more than eight hundred twenty thousand from monopoly wine, and more than two million seven hundred eighty thousand from salt profits."
translations.idiomatic: Revenue reported that after the He-Huang reconquest annual cash receipts exceeded 9.25 million strings—5.55 million in taxes, 820,000 in liquor monopoly, 2.78 million in salt."

sentences.zh: 宣宗元聖至明成武獻文睿智章仁神聰懿道大孝皇帝下大中八年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuānzong (posthumous titles)—the latter part of his reign; eighth year of the Dazhong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuānzong (posthumous titles)—the latter part of his reign; eighth year of the Dazhong era (

sentences.zh: 甲戌，公元八五四年）

translations.literal: jiaxu, corresponding to 854 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiaxu, 854 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月丙戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the bingxu new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the bingxu new moon, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 罷元會。

translations.literal: The New Year assembly was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The New Year audience was canceled.

sentences.zh: 上自即位以來，治弒憲宗之黨，宦官、外戚乃至東宮官屬，誅竄甚眾。

translations.literal: From the time the emperor ascended the throne, he had punished the faction that murdered Emperor Xianzong—eunuchs, maternal kin, and even Eastern Palace officials; very many were executed and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Since his accession he had purged those implicated in Emperor Xianzong's murder—eunuchs, in-laws, even Eastern Palace staff—in vast numbers.

sentences.zh: 慮人情不安，丙申，詔：「長慶之初，亂臣賊子，頃搜擿餘黨，流竄已盡，其餘族從疏遠者，一切不問。」

translations.literal: Fearing that popular sentiment was unsettled, on bingshen an edict stated: "In the beginning of the Changqing era, rebellious ministers and traitorous sons—recently the remaining partisans were sought out and banished, and they are now exhausted; as for more distant clan and kin, all are without inquiry."
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, fearing public unease, he proclaimed: "Changqing rebels have been hunted to exhaustion; distant kin are now forgiven."

sentences.zh: 二月，中書門下奏拾遺、補闕缺員，請更增補。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized that remonstrance and supplementation posts were vacant and requested further appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Secretariat asked to fill vacant remonstrance and supplementation posts.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「諫官要在舉職，不必人多，如張道符、牛叢、趙璘輩數人，使朕日聞所不聞足矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Remonstrating officials must perform their duties; there is no need for many men—as with Zhang Daofu, Niu Cong, Zhao Lin, and a few others, if each day I hear what I have not heard, that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "A few good remonstrators suffice—Zhang Daofu, Niu Cong, Zhao Lin give me daily what I need to hear."

sentences.zh: 叢，僧孺之子也。

translations.literal: Cong was a son of Niu Sengru.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was Niu Sengru's son.

sentences.zh: 久之，叢自司勳員外郎出為睦州刺史，入謝，上賜之紫。

translations.literal: After a long time, Cong went out from director in the Ministry of Personnel to prefect of Mu; entering to give thanks, the emperor bestowed purple on him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cong left a Ministry of Personnel post for Mu Prefecture; at his farewell audience the emperor granted him purple.

sentences.zh: 叢既謝，前言曰：「臣所服緋，刺史所借也。」

translations.literal: After Cong had given thanks, he spoke earlier, saying, "The scarlet I wear is borrowed from the prefect."
translations.idiomatic: Cong added: "This scarlet robe is the prefect's loan."

sentences.zh: 上遽曰：「且賜緋。」

translations.literal: The emperor hastily said, "For the present, scarlet is bestowed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor quickly said, "Then keep scarlet."

sentences.zh: 上重惜服章，有司常具緋、紫衣數襲從行，以備賞賜，或半歲不用其一，故當時以緋、紫為榮。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly treasured regalia; the relevant offices constantly prepared several sets of scarlet and purple garments to follow on his journeys, ready for bestowal; sometimes half a year would pass without using one—therefore at the time scarlet and purple were regarded as honor.
translations.idiomatic: He prized court dress so highly that attendants carried spare scarlet and purple robes on tour; grants were rare, which made those colors a mark of honor.

sentences.zh: 上重翰林學士，至於遷官，必校歲月，以為不可以官爵私近臣也。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly valued Hanlin academicians; as for their promotions, he always checked the months and years, holding that rank and office must not be used to favor close ministers privately.
translations.idiomatic: He valued Hanlin scholars so highly that he tracked their tenure month by month, refusing to reward favorites with rank.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，丙戌，以右散騎常侍高少逸為陝虢觀察使。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on bingxu, Right Regular Attendant Gao Shaoyi was made observer of Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, on bingxu, Gao Shaoyi was appointed observer of Shan-Guo.

sentences.zh: 有敕使過硤石，怒餅黑，鞭驛吏見血。

translations.literal: A dispatch envoy passed Xia Gorge, grew angry that the cakes were black, and flogged the post-house clerk until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: A palace envoy passing Xia Gorge, furious that his cakes were burnt, whipped the post clerk until he bled.

sentences.zh: 少逸封其餅以進。

translations.literal: Shaoyi sealed the cakes and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi sealed those cakes and sent them up to court.

sentences.zh: 敕使還，上責之曰：「深山中如此食豈易得！」

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, the emperor rebuked him, saying, "In deep mountains such food is not easily obtained!"
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy returned, the emperor rebuked him: "In the deep mountains such food is hard to come by!"

sentences.zh: 謫配恭陵。

translations.literal: He was banished to serve at Gongling.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished to Gongling.

sentences.zh: 立皇子洽為懷王，汭為昭王，汶為康王。

translations.literal: The emperor's sons Qia was established as Prince of Huai, Rui as Prince of Zhao, and Wen as Prince of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Qia, Rui, and Wen were enfeoffed as Huai, Zhao, and Kang respectively.

sentences.zh: 上獵於苑北，遇樵夫，問其縣，曰：「涇陽人也。」

translations.literal: The emperor hunted north of the park and met a woodcutter; he asked his county, and the man said, "I am a man of Jingyang."
translations.idiomatic: Hunting north of the imperial park, he met a woodcutter who said he was from Jingyang."

sentences.zh: 「令為誰？」

translations.literal: "Who is the magistrate?"
translations.idiomatic: "Who is your magistrate?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「李行言。」

translations.literal: The man said, "Li Xingyan."
translations.idiomatic: "Li Xingyan," he replied."

sentences.zh: 「為政何如？」

translations.literal: "How is his governance?"
translations.idiomatic: "And his governance?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「性執。

translations.literal: The man said, "He is obstinate by nature.
translations.idiomatic: "Stubborn," said the woodcutter.

sentences.zh: 有強盜數人，軍家索之，竟不與，盡殺之。」

translations.literal: There were several strong robbers; military households demanded them, but he would not hand them over and killed them all."
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers demanded several bandits, he refused and killed them all."

sentences.zh: 上歸，帖其名於寢殿之柱。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, he pasted the man's name on a pillar of his sleeping hall.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he pasted Xingyan's name on a bedroom pillar.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，行言除海州刺史，入謝。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Xingyan was made prefect of Haizhou and entered to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Xingyan was appointed prefect of Haizhou and came to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 上賜之金紫，問曰：「卿知所以衣紫乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed gold and purple on him and asked, "Do you know why you wear purple?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him gold and purple and asked whether he knew why."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「不知。」

translations.literal: He replied, "I do not know."
translations.idiomatic: "I do not," he answered."

sentences.zh: 上命取殿柱之貼示之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the posting on the hall pillar to be shown him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed him the pillar posting.

sentences.zh: 上以甘露之變，惟李訓、鄭注當死，自餘王涯、賈餗等無罪，詔皆雪其冤。

translations.literal: Because of the Sweet Dew Incident, only Li Xun and Zheng Zhu should die; the rest—Wang Ya, Jia Su, and the others—were without guilt; an edict cleared all their wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: After the Sweet Dew Incident the emperor held that only Li Xun and Zheng Zhu deserved death; Wang Ya, Jia Su, and the rest were posthumously cleared.

sentences.zh: 上召翰林學士韋澳，托以論詩，屏左右與之語曰：「近日外間謂內侍權勢何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Hanlin Academician Wei Ao, using discussion of poetry as a pretext, dismissed attendants, and said to him, "Recently outside they say—how are the inner attendants' powers?"
translations.idiomatic: Summoning Hanlin scholar Wei Ao under pretense of discussing poetry, the emperor dismissed attendants and asked what people said of the eunuchs' power."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下威斷，非前朝之比。」

translations.literal: Ao replied, "Your Majesty's decisive authority is not comparable to the previous dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty's authority far exceeds the previous reign," Ao replied."

sentences.zh: 上閉目搖首曰：「全未，全未！

translations.literal: The emperor closed his eyes and shook his head, saying, "Not at all, not at all!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shut his eyes and shook his head: "Not at all!

sentences.zh: 尚畏之在。

translations.literal: They are still feared as present.
translations.idiomatic: They are still feared.

sentences.zh: 卿謂策將安在！」

translations.literal: Where do you say the stratagem lies!"
translations.idiomatic: Where then is your strategy?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「若與外廷議之，恐有太和之變，不若就其中擇有才識者與之謀。」

translations.literal: Ao replied, "If discussed with the outer court, I fear there will be a change like that of the Taihe era; better to choose men of talent and insight among them and plot with them."
translations.idiomatic: "Consulting the outer court risks another Taihe disaster," Ao said; "better to win over talented eunuchs."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此乃末策。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "That is the least of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: "That is the worst stratagem," said the emperor.

sentences.zh: 朕已試之矣，自衣黃、衣綠至衣緋，皆感恩，才衣紫則相與為一矣！」

translations.literal: I have already tried it—from yellow robes, green robes, to scarlet, all were grateful; once they wore purple they united as one!"
translations.idiomatic: I have tried it—from yellow to green to scarlet they were loyal; in purple they became one bloc!"

sentences.zh: 上又嘗與令狐綯謀盡誅宦官，恐濫及無辜，密奏曰：「但有罪勿捨，有闕勿補，自然漸耗，至於盡矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor also once plotted with Linghu Tao to execute all eunuchs; fearing harm to the innocent, Tao secretly memorialized, "Only do not spare the guilty, do not fill vacancies—naturally they will gradually diminish until exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: He also plotted with Linghu Tao to exterminate the eunuchs; Tao secretly urged: punish the guilty, fill no vacancies, and their numbers will dwindle."

sentences.zh: 宦者竊見其奏，由是益與朝士相惡，南北司如水火矣。

translations.literal: The eunuchs secretly saw the memorial; therefore they grew even more hostile to court officials; northern and southern bureaus were like fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs who read the memorial grew more hostile; court and palace factions became fire and water.

sentences.zh: 宣宗元聖至明成武獻文睿智章仁神聰懿道大孝皇帝下大中九年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuānzong (posthumous titles)—the latter part of his reign; ninth year of the Dazhong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuānzong (posthumous titles)—the latter part of his reign; ninth year of the Dazhong era (

sentences.zh: 乙亥，公元八五五年）

translations.literal: yihai, corresponding to 855 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yihai, 855 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲申，成德軍奏節度使王元逵薨，軍中立其子節度副使紹鼎。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiashen, the Chengde Army reported that military commissioner Wang Yuankui had died and the army had established his son, deputy commissioner Wang Shaoding.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on jiashen, Chengde reported Wang Yuankui's death and the army's elevation of his son Shaoding.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以紹鼎為成德留後。

translations.literal: On guimao, Shaoding was made acting commissioner of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Shaoding became acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二月，以醴泉令李君奭為懷州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second month, Magistrate of Liquan Li Junyi was made prefect of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Li Junyi of Liquan was made prefect of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，上校獵渭上，有父老以十數，聚於佛祠。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was reviewing hunts on the Wei River, more than ten elders had gathered at a Buddhist shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, hunting on the Wei, he had met a dozen elders at a temple.

sentences.zh: 上問之，對曰：「醴泉百姓也。

translations.literal: The emperor asked them; they replied, "We are people of Liquan County.
translations.idiomatic: “They said they were from Liquan.

sentences.zh: 縣令李君奭有異政，考滿當罷，詣府乞留，故此祈佛，冀諧所願耳。」

translations.literal: Magistrate Li Junyi has exceptional administration; when his term ended he should have been removed, but we went to the prefecture begging he remain—therefore we pray to the Buddha, hoping our wish may be fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Li Junyi governed so well that when his term ended we begged the prefecture to keep him—hence this prayer."

sentences.zh: 及懷州刺史闕，上手筆除君奭，宰相莫之測。

translations.literal: When the post of Huaizhou prefect fell vacant, the emperor personally wrote Junyi's appointment; the chief ministers could not fathom it.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaizhou fell vacant the emperor personally appointed Junyi, baffling his ministers.

sentences.zh: 君奭入謝，上以此獎厲，眾始知之。

translations.literal: Junyi entered to give thanks; the emperor used this to encourage him—only then did the multitude learn of it.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience the emperor explained the Liquan episode, and all understood.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔邠寧節度使畢諴還邠州。

translations.literal: In the third month, an edict ordered military commissioner of Binning Bi Xie to return to Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Bi Xie was ordered back to Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先是，以河、湟初附，党項未平，移邠寧軍於寧州。

translations.literal: Earlier, because the He and Huang region had newly submitted and the Tangut were not yet pacified, the Binning army had been moved to Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, with He-Huang newly recovered and Tangut unrest, Binning troops had been shifted to Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 至是，南山、平夏、党項皆安，威、鹽、武三州軍食足，故令還理所。

translations.literal: By now the Southern Mountain, Pingxia, and Tangut were all settled, and military grain in Wei, Yan, and Wu prefectures was sufficient; therefore they were ordered back to their original seat.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Tangut affairs were quiet and frontier granaries full, the army returned to its old headquarters.

sentences.zh: 夏，閏四月，詔以「州縣差役不均，自今每縣據人貧富及役輕重作差科簿，送刺史檢署訖，鎖於令廳，每有役事委令，據簿輪差。」

translations.literal: In summer, the intercalary fourth month, an edict stated, "Corvée assignments in prefectures and counties are uneven; henceforth each county shall compile a register of corvée according to people's wealth and the lightness or heaviness of duties, send it to the prefect for inspection and endorsement, lock it in the magistrate's hall, and for each corvée task the magistrate shall rotate assignments according to the register."
translations.idiomatic: An intercalary-fourth-month edict required counties to rank corvée by wealth and duty weight, file registers with prefects, and rotate assignments fairly."

sentences.zh: 五月，丙寅，以王紹鼎為成德節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on bingyin, Wang Shaoding was made military commissioner of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingyin, Shaoding received full commission as Chengde military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上聰察強記，宮中廝役給灑掃者，皆能識其姓名，才性所任，呼召使令，無差誤者。

translations.literal: The emperor was perceptive and had a strong memory; palace attendants who sprinkled and swept—he could all recognize their names, talents, and suitable posts; summoning and commanding them, there were no errors.
translations.idiomatic: So sharp was his memory that he knew every palace servant's name, talent, and proper task.

sentences.zh: 天下奏獄吏卒姓名，一覽皆記之。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm, memorials on prisoners and clerks' names—one glance and he remembered them all.
translations.idiomatic: He could memorize at a glance every prisoner and clerk named in empire-wide reports.

sentences.zh: 度支奏漬污帛，誤書「漬」為「清」，樞密承旨孫隱中謂上不之見，輒足成之，及中書復入，上怒，推按擅改章奏者罰謫之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue reported stained silk; "stained" was mistakenly written as "clear"; Grand Council Secretariat bearer Sun Yinzhong thought the emperor had not seen it and simply added a foot to complete the character; when it reentered the Secretariat, the emperor was angry and investigated and punished those who had altered memorials on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Revenue miswrote "stained" as "clear," Sun Yinzhong altered the character; the emperor discovered it and punished unauthorized tampering with memorials.

sentences.zh: 上密令翰林學士韋澳纂次諸州境土風物及諸利害為一書，自寫而上之，雖子弟不知也，號曰《處分語》。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly ordered Hanlin Academician Wei Ao to compile the territory, local products, and advantages and disadvantages of each prefecture into one book, write it himself, and submit it upward; even his sons did not know of it; it was titled "Disposition Words."
translations.idiomatic: He secretly had Wei Ao compile a handbook on every prefecture's terrain and interests—the "Disposition Words"—unknown even to Wei's family.

sentences.zh: 他日，鄧州刺史薛弘宗入謝，出，謂澳曰：「上處分本州事驚人。」

translations.literal: Another day, Prefect of Dengzhou Xue Hongzong entered to give thanks; leaving, he said to Ao, "The emperor's dispositions on our prefecture's affairs are astonishing."
translations.idiomatic: “When Dengzhou prefect Xue Hongzong thanked the emperor, he told Ao he was astonished at how much the throne knew about his circuit.”

sentences.zh: 澳詢之，皆《處分語》中事也。

translations.literal: Ao inquired; all were matters in the "Disposition Words."
translations.idiomatic: Ao found every detail came from that secret book.

sentences.zh: 澳在翰林，上或遣中使宣旨草詔。

translations.literal: While Ao was in the Hanlin, the emperor sometimes sent palace envoys to announce orders to draft edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hanlin, palace envoys sometimes ordered Ao to draft edicts.

sentences.zh: 事有不可者，澳輒曰：「茲事須降御札，方敢施行。」

translations.literal: When something could not be done, Ao would say, "This matter requires an imperial autograph before it may be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: “If an order was improper, Ao insisted on an autograph edict.”

sentences.zh: 淹留至旦，上疏論之，上多從之。

translations.literal: He would delay until dawn and memorialize on it; the emperor mostly followed his views.
translations.idiomatic: He delayed until dawn, memorialized, and usually prevailed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，浙東軍亂，逐觀察使李訥。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Zhedong army mutinied and drove out observer Li Na.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhedong troops mutinied and expelled observer Li Na.

sentences.zh: 訥，遜之弟子也，性卞急，遇將士不以禮，故亂作。

translations.literal: Na was a disciple of Li Xun's nephew; by nature he was harsh and impatient and did not treat officers and soldiers with courtesy—therefore the mutiny arose.
translations.idiomatic: Na, kin to Li Xun's family, ruled harshly and drove his men to revolt.

sentences.zh: 淮南饑，民多流亡，節度使杜悰荒於游宴，政事不治。
