translations.literal: Huainan suffered famine; many people fled; military commissioner Du Cong was dissolute in feasting and hunting and did not govern affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan starved and people fled while Du Cong feasted and neglected government.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，甲午，以門下侍郎、同平章事崔鉉同平章事，充淮南節度使。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this, on jiawu he made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal Chief Minister Cui Xuan Co-Equal Chief Minister and military commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the emperor sent chief minister Cui Xuan to replace Du Cong in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以悰為太子太傅、分司。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Cong was made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent with a separate office.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Cong was sidelined as grand tutor with a sinecure.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙亥，貶李訥為朗州刺史，監軍王宗景杖四十，配恭陵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yihai, Li Na was demoted to prefect of Langzhou; army supervisor Wang Zongjing was flogged forty strokes and assigned to Gongling.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Na was demoted to Langzhou; supervisor Wang Zongjing was flogged and banished to Gongling.

sentences.zh: 仍詔「自今戎臣失律，並坐監軍。」

translations.literal: An edict further stated, "From now on when military ministers violate discipline, the army supervisors shall also be punished."
translations.idiomatic: A new rule punished army supervisors whenever generals broke discipline."

sentences.zh: 以禮部侍郎沈詢為浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Shen Xun was made observer of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xun was sent as observer of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 詢，傳師之子也。

translations.literal: Xun was a son of Shen Chuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was Shen Chuanshi's son.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，以吏部侍郎柳仲郢為兵部侍郎，充鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, Vice Minister of Personnel Liu Zhongyi was made Vice Minister of War and salt and iron transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, Liu Zhongyi became vice minister of war and salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 有閭閻醫工劉集因緣交通禁中，上敕鹽鐵補場官。

translations.literal: A neighborhood physician, Liu Ji, by connections entered the inner palace; the emperor ordered the salt office to appoint him to a field post.
translations.idiomatic: Physician Liu Ji curried favor in the palace and was ordered appointed to a salt-field post.

sentences.zh: 仲郢上言：「醫工術精，宜補醫官。

translations.literal: Zhongyi memorialized, "Physicians skilled in medicine should be appointed medical officials.
translations.idiomatic: “Zhongyi protested: physicians belong in medical offices.

sentences.zh: 若委務銅鹽，何以課其殿最！

translations.literal: If entrusted with copper and salt affairs, how can their performance be graded!
translations.idiomatic: Salt posts measure revenue—how can we grade a doctor's work?

sentences.zh: 且場官賤品，非特敕所宜親，臣未敢奉詔！」

translations.literal: Moreover, field posts are low in rank—not what special edicts should personally touch; I dare not accept the order!"
translations.idiomatic: Field posts are too low for imperial favor—I dare not obey!"

sentences.zh: 上遽批：「劉集宜賜絹百匹，遣之。」

translations.literal: The emperor quickly wrote in the margin, "Liu Ji should be granted one hundred bolts of silk and dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor annotated: grant Liu Ji silk and send him away."

sentences.zh: 他日，見仲郢，勞之曰：「卿論劉集事甚佳。」

translations.literal: Another day, seeing Zhongyi, he praised him, saying, "Your discussion of Liu Ji's affair was excellent."
translations.idiomatic: “Later he praised Zhongyi's stand on Liu Ji.”

sentences.zh: 上嘗若不能食，召醫工梁新診脈，治之數日，良已。

translations.literal: The emperor once seemed unable to eat; he summoned the physician Liang Xin to feel his pulse; after several days of treatment he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor lost his appetite, physician Liang Xin cured him in days.

sentences.zh: 新因自陳求官，上不許，但敕鹽鐵使月給錢三十緡而已。

translations.literal: Xin thereupon asked for an office himself; the emperor did not consent but only ordered the salt commissioner to give thirty strings of cash per month.
translations.idiomatic: Xin then sought office; the emperor refused but paid him thirty strings monthly from salt funds.

sentences.zh: 右威衛大將軍康季榮前為涇原節度使，擅用官錢二萬緡，事覺，季榮請以家財償之。

translations.literal: General of the Right Weiwu Kang Jirong had formerly been military commissioner of Jingyuan and on his own authority used twenty thousand strings of official money; when the matter came to light, Jirong asked to repay from family property.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Jirong, ex-commissioner of Jingyuan, had embezzled twenty thousand strings and offered family wealth to repay.

sentences.zh: 上以季榮有開河、湟功，許之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Jirong had merit in opening the He and Huang region, consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, honoring his He-Huang service, agreed.

sentences.zh: 給事中封還敕書，諫官亦上言。

translations.literal: A drafting reviewer returned the edict; remonstrating officials also memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The drafting office returned the edict; censors protested.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚辰，貶季榮夔州長史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengchen, Jirong was demoted to long secretary of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengchen, Jirong was demoted to Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 江西觀察使鄭祗德以其子顥尚主通顯，固求散地，甲午，以祗德為賓客、分司。

translations.literal: Observer of Jiangxi Zheng Qide, because his son Hao had married the princess and gained prominence, firmly sought a post away from court; on jiawu he was made guest of the heir apparent with a separate office.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qide, whose son had married a princess, begged a quiet post and was made a ceremonial attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 宣宗元聖至明成武獻文睿智章仁神聰懿道大孝皇帝下大中十年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuānzong (posthumous titles)—the latter part of his reign; tenth year of the Dazhong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuānzong (posthumous titles)—the latter part of his reign; tenth year of the Dazhong era (

sentences.zh: 丙子，公元八五六年）

translations.literal: bingzi, corresponding to 856 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingzi, 856 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁巳，以御史大夫鄭朗為工部尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingsi, Censor-in-Chief Zheng Lang was made Minister of Works and Co-Equal Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on dingsi, Zheng Lang joined the chief ministers as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 上命裴休極言時事，休請早建太子，上曰：「若建太子，則朕遂為閒人。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Pei Xiu to speak exhaustively on current affairs; Xiu requested early establishment of the heir apparent; the emperor said, "If the heir apparent is established, then I become a man of leisure."
translations.idiomatic: Asked for candid counsel, Pei Xiu urged naming an heir; the emperor snapped that a crown prince would make him idle."

sentences.zh: 休不敢復言。

translations.literal: Xiu did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu fell silent.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙戌，休以疾辭位，不許。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingxu, Xiu pleaded illness to resign office; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Xiu tried to resign for illness but was refused.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛亥，詔以「回鶻有功於國，世為婚姻，稱臣奉貢，北邊無警。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinhai, an edict stated, "The Uyghurs rendered merit to the state; for generations we have been joined in marriage; they called themselves subjects and offered tribute; the northern border was without alarm.
translations.idiomatic: “In the third month an edict recalled Uyghur loyalty and marriage ties.

sentences.zh: 會昌中虜廷喪亂，可汗奔亡，屬奸臣當軸，遽加殄滅。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era the barbarian court fell into disorder; the qaghan fled; wicked ministers held power and hastened their destruction.
translations.idiomatic: During Huichang their court collapsed and a wicked minister destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 近有降者雲，已厖歷今為可汗，尚寓安西，俟其歸復牙帳，當加冊命。」

translations.literal: Recently a surrendering man said that Pangtekin is now qaghan, still dwelling in Anxi; when he returns to restore his encampment, investiture and appointment shall be added."
translations.idiomatic: Refugees say Pangtekin still lives in Anxi as qaghan and will receive investiture when he returns."

sentences.zh: 上以京兆久不理，夏，五月，丁卯，以翰林學士、工部侍郎韋澳為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Because the capital district had long gone ungoverned, in summer, the fifth month, on dingmao, Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Works Wei Ao was made prefect of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, Wei Ao was made capital prefect to clean up the neglected metropolis.

sentences.zh: 澳為人公直，既視事，豪貴斂手。

translations.literal: Ao was upright by nature; once he took office, the powerful shrank back.
translations.idiomatic: Ao was famously upright; the mighty feared him at once.

sentences.zh: 鄭光莊吏恣橫，為閭裡患，積年租稅不入，澳執而械之。

translations.literal: Zheng Guang's estate managers were overbearing and were a neighborhood scourge; for years rents and taxes did not enter; Ao seized and shackled them.
translations.idiomatic: Ao shackled the bullying rent agents on Zheng Guang's estates who had withheld taxes for years.

sentences.zh: 上於延英問澳，澳具奏其狀。

translations.literal: At Yanying the emperor asked Ao; Ao reported the full circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanying Hall the emperor questioned him; Ao told the whole story.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿何以處之？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "How will you deal with them?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked how he would punish them."

sentences.zh: 澳曰：「欲置於法。」

translations.literal: Ao said, "I intend to place them within the law."
translations.idiomatic: "By law," Ao said."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「鄭光甚愛之，何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Zheng Guang loves them greatly—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: "But Zheng Guang loves them," said the emperor."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下自內庭用臣為京兆，欲以清畿甸之積弊，若鄭光莊吏積年為蠹，得寬重辟，是陛下之法獨行於貧戶耳，臣未敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty used me from the inner court as capital prefect, wishing to clear accumulated abuses of the capital region; if Zheng Guang's estate managers, who for years have been pests, receive a light penalty, then Your Majesty's law runs only against poor households—I dare not accept the order."
translations.idiomatic: "You made me prefect to purge capital abuses," Ao replied; "if Guang's men get light punishment, the law applies only to the poor—I cannot obey."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「誠如此。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "It is indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: "True," said the emperor.

sentences.zh: 但鄭光□帶我不置，卿與痛杖，貸其死，可乎？」

translations.literal: But Zheng Guang importunes me without cease—you give them a severe flogging and spare their lives, can you?"
translations.idiomatic: Guang will not stop pleading—flog them hard but spare their lives, can you?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣不敢不奉詔，願聽臣且系之，俟征足及釋之。」

translations.literal: He replied, "I dare not fail to accept the order; I beg to detain them for now and release them when rents are paid in full."
translations.idiomatic: "I obey," Ao said, "but let me hold them until all rents are paid."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「灼然可。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "That is clearly acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: "That will do," said the emperor.

sentences.zh: 朕為鄭光故撓卿法，殊以為愧。」

translations.literal: For Zheng Guang's sake I bent your law—it shames me deeply."
translations.idiomatic: I twisted the law for Zheng Guang; I am deeply ashamed."

sentences.zh: 澳歸府，即杖之。

translations.literal: Ao returned to his yamen and at once had them flogged.
translations.idiomatic: Ao went straight home and had them beaten.

sentences.zh: 督租數百斛足，乃以吏歸光。

translations.literal: When several hundred piculs of rent were collected in full, he returned the managers to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Once hundreds of piculs of back rent were paid, he sent the agents back to Guang.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊寅，以中書侍郎、同平章事裴休同平章事，充宣武節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wuyin, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal Chief Minister Pei Xiu was made Co-Equal Chief Minister and military commissioner of Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, wuyin: Pei Xiu, vice director and chief minister, became Xuanwu military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 司農卿韋廑欲求夏州節度使，有術士知之，詣廑門曰：「吾善醮星辰，求官無不如意。」

translations.literal: Minister of Agriculture Wei Yin wished to become military commissioner of Xia Prefecture; a magician learned of it and came to Yin's gate, saying, "I am skilled at offering sacrifices to the stars—petitions for office never fail."
translations.idiomatic: “Wei Yin wanted Xiazhou; a sorcerer promised star-altar rites that always won offices.”

sentences.zh: 廑信之，夜，設醮具於庭。

translations.literal: Yin believed him; that night ritual implements were set out in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Yin believed him and set up the altar in his courtyard that night.

sentences.zh: 術士曰：「請公自書官階一通。」

translations.literal: The magician said, "Please write out one full statement of the office you seek."
translations.idiomatic: “The sorcerer asked Yin to write his desired rank on a slip.”

sentences.zh: 既得之，仰天大呼曰：「韋廑有異志，令我祭天。」

translations.literal: When he had it, he shouted to heaven, "Wei Yin harbors rebellious intent and ordered me to sacrifice to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: “With the slip in hand he cried out that Yin was plotting treason and had him sacrifice to Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 廑舉家拜泣曰：「願山人賜百口之命！」

translations.literal: The whole household bowed and wept, saying, "We beg the mountain lord to grant our hundred lives!"
translations.idiomatic: “The family wept and begged the sorcerer to spare all their lives.”

sentences.zh: 家之貨財珍玩盡與之。

translations.literal: The household's goods and precious curios were all given to him.
translations.idiomatic: They gave him their entire fortune in valuables.

sentences.zh: 邏者怪術士服鮮衣，執以為盜。

translations.literal: Patrol guards thought it strange that the magician wore fine clothes and seized him as a thief.
translations.idiomatic: Patrolmen arrested the richly dressed sorcerer as a thief.

sentences.zh: 術士急，乃曰：「韋廑令我祭天，我欲告之，彼以家財求我耳。」

translations.literal: The magician, in haste, then said, "Wei Yin had me sacrifice to Heaven; when I meant to report him, he bought me off with his family wealth."
translations.idiomatic: “Cornered, he claimed Yin had bribed him to perform the rite and then silenced him.”

sentences.zh: 事上聞，秋，九月，上召廑面詰之，具知其冤，謂宰相曰：「韋廑城南甲族，為奸人所誣，勿使獄吏辱之。」

translations.literal: When the matter reached the throne, in autumn, the ninth month, the emperor summoned Yin and questioned him face to face; he learned the full injustice and told the chief ministers, "Wei Yin is a leading clan south of the capital—do not let prison clerks humiliate him."
translations.idiomatic: “Autumn, ninth month: the emperor heard Yin out, saw he was framed, and forbade the jailers to disgrace a great southern clan.”

sentences.zh: 立以術士付京兆，杖死，貶廑永州司馬。

translations.literal: He immediately handed the magician to the capital prefect, who beat him to death, and demoted Yin to vice-governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer was flogged to death in the capital; Yin was demoted to Yongzhou vice-governor.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎、判戶部、附馬都尉鄭顥營求作相甚切。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue, acting commissioner of revenue, and imperial son-in-law Zheng Hao eagerly sought to become chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Hao, revenue vice minister and imperial son-in-law, campaigned hard for the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 其父祗德聞之，與書曰：「聞汝已判戶部，是吾必死之年；

translations.literal: His father Zhide heard of it and wrote him, "I hear you already hold acting charge of the Ministry of Revenue—that is the year I must die;
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhide wrote: "You now run Revenue—that is the year I die;

sentences.zh: 又聞欲求宰相，是吾必死之日也。」

translations.literal: and I hear you wish to become chief minister—that is the day I must die."
translations.idiomatic: and if you seek the chancellorship, that is the day I die."

sentences.zh: 顥懼，累表辭劇務。

translations.literal: Hao was afraid and repeatedly memorialized to resign heavy duties.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Hao repeatedly asked to be relieved of heavy office.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙酉，以顥為秘書監。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yiyou, Hao was made director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, yiyou: Hao was made palace librarian.

sentences.zh: 上遣使詣安西鎮撫回鶻，使者至靈武，會回鶻可漢遣使入貢。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to pacify the Uyghurs in Anxi; when the envoys reached Lingwu, they encountered an Uyghur qaghan's envoy entering to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys sent to soothe Anxi met a Uyghur tribute mission at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛亥，冊拜為嗢祿登裡羅汩沒密施合俱錄毘伽懷建可汗，以衛尉少卿王端章充使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinhai, he was enfeoffed as Qaghan Ulug Elug Bolmish Qapghan Khagan of the restored state; Vice Director of the Imperial Guard Wang Duanzhang was sent as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, xinhai: the Uyghur ruler was invested as restored qaghan; Wang Duanzhang bore the patent.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李景讓上言：「穆宗乃陛下兄，敬宗、文宗、武宗乃兄之子，陛下拜兄尚可，拜侄可乎！

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Li Jingrang submitted, "Emperor Muzong was Your Majesty's elder brother; Emperors Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong were your brother's sons—can Your Majesty bow to a nephew?
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Li Jingrang submitted, "Emperor Muzong was Your Majesty's elder brother; Emperors Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong were your brother's sons. It may be acceptable for Your Majesty to bow to an elder brother, but can you bow to nephews?

sentences.zh: 是使陛下不得親事七廟也，宜遷四主出太廟，還代宗以下入廟。」

translations.literal: That would prevent Your Majesty from personally serving the seven temples; the four [recent] rulers should be moved out of the Grand Temple and Emperor Daizong and those below should be restored."
translations.idiomatic: This would keep Your Majesty from personally serving the seven temples. The four spirit-tablets should be moved out of the Grand Temple, and Daizong and the emperors below him restored to the temple."

sentences.zh: 詔百官議其事，不決而止。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all officials to debate the matter; no decision was reached and it was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Officials debated by edict but reached no decision.

sentences.zh: 時人以是薄景讓。

translations.literal: People of the time despised Jingrang for this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries looked down on Jingrang.

sentences.zh: 敕「於靈感、會善二寺置戒壇，諸僧、尼應填闕者委長老僧選擇，給公賃，赴兩壇受戒，兩京各選大德十人主其事。

translations.literal: An edict read, "At the ordination platforms of Linggan and Huishan Monasteries, monks and nuns filling vacancies shall be chosen by senior monks, given public stipends, and sent to the two platforms to receive the precepts; ten great monks in each capital shall preside.
translations.idiomatic: “An edict centralized ordination at two monasteries under senior monks' selection.

sentences.zh: 有不堪者罷之，堪者給牒，遣歸本州。

translations.literal: Those unfit were dismissed; the fit were given certificates and sent back to their home prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Unfit candidates were rejected; fit ones received licenses and went home.

sentences.zh: 不見戒壇公牒，毋得私容。

translations.literal: Without the platforms' public certificates, none might be privately admitted.
translations.idiomatic: Private ordinations without platform certificates were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 仍先選舊僧、尼，舊僧、尼無堪者，乃選外人。」

translations.literal: Former monks and nuns were to be chosen first; only if none were fit were outsiders chosen."
translations.idiomatic: Veteran clergy were preferred; outsiders filled gaps only."

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以戶部侍郎、判戶部崔慎由為工部尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: On renchen, Vice Minister of Revenue and acting commissioner of revenue Cui Shenyou was made Minister of Works and Co-Equal Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Renchen: Cui Shenyou became works minister and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 上每命相，左右無知者。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor appointed a chief minister, those close at hand knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named chancellors without telling his attendants.

sentences.zh: 前此一日，令樞密宣旨於學士院，以兵部侍郎、判度支蕭鄴同平章事。

translations.literal: The day before, he had the Bureau of Military Affairs announce to the Hanlin Academy that Vice Minister of War and acting commissioner of fiscal affairs Xiao Ye was made Co-Equal Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: A day earlier Xiao Ye's appointment had been drafted for the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 樞密使王歸長、馬公儒覆奏：「鄴所判度支應罷否？」

translations.literal: Military commissioners Wang Guichang and Ma Gongru reported back, "Should Ye's charge of fiscal affairs be removed?"
translations.idiomatic: “The commissioners asked whether Xiao Ye would keep fiscal affairs.”

sentences.zh: 上以為歸長等佑之，即手書慎由名及新命付學士院，仍云「落判戶部事」。

translations.literal: The emperor thought Guichang and the others were protecting Ye; he at once wrote Shenyou's name and the new appointment by hand for the Hanlin Academy, adding "remove acting charge of revenue."
translations.idiomatic: “Thinking they favored Xiao Ye, the emperor wrote in Cui Shenyou instead and stripped Ye of revenue.”

sentences.zh: 鄴，明之八世孫也。

translations.literal: Ye was a descendant in the eighth generation of [Emperor] Ming [of Han].
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ye was Ming of Han's eighth-generation descendant.

sentences.zh: 內園使李敬寔遇鄭郎不避馬，郎奏之。

translations.literal: Inner Park Commissioner Li Jingshi met a cavalier of the heir apparent and did not yield the road; the cavalier reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingshi refused to give way to an heir-apparent cavalier, who complained.

sentences.zh: 上責敬寔，對曰：「供奉官例不避。」

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Jingshi; he replied, "By regulation palace commissioners need not yield."
translations.idiomatic: “Rebuked, Jingshi cited the exemption for palace commissioners.”

sentences.zh: 上曰：「汝銜敕命，橫絕可也，豈得私出而不避宰相乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You carry imperial orders and may cross as you please—but how can you go out privately and not yield to a chief minister!"
translations.idiomatic: “The emperor said imperial orders allowed passage, not private outings that ignored chancellors.”

sentences.zh: 命剝色，配南牙。

translations.literal: He ordered his colored robe stripped and assigned him to the southern guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshi was stripped of rank and sent to the southern guard.

sentences.zh: 宣宗元聖至明成武獻文睿智章仁神聰懿道大孝皇帝下大中十一年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuānzong, the Yuan, Sheng, Zhi, Ming, Cheng, Wu, Xian, Wen, Rui, Zhi, Zhang, Ren, Shen, Cong, Yi, Dao, Great Filial Emperor (posthumous titles)—below; eleventh year of the Dazhong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuānzong—below; Dazhong year eleven (

sentences.zh: 丁丑，公元八五七年）

translations.literal: dingchou, corresponding to 857 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dingchou, 857 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙午，以御史中丞兼尚書右丞夏侯孜為戶部侍郎、判戶部事。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on bingwu, Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat Xiahou Zi was made Vice Minister of Revenue and acting commissioner of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, first month, bingwu: Xiahou Zi took charge of revenue.

sentences.zh: 先是，判戶部有缺，京兆尹韋澳奏事，上欲以澳補之。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been a vacancy in acting charge of revenue; when Capital Prefect Wei Ao reported to court, the emperor wished to fill it with Ao.
translations.idiomatic: A revenue vacancy opened; the emperor wanted Wei Ao for it.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「臣比年心力衰耗，難以處繁劇，屢就陛下乞小鎮，聖恩未許。」

translations.literal: He declined, saying, "In recent years my mind and strength have waned and I can hardly bear heavy duties; I have repeatedly begged Your Majesty for a small frontier post, but the sacred favor has not been granted."
translations.idiomatic: “Ao pleaded age and fatigue and asked again for a minor frontier post.”

sentences.zh: 上不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 及歸，其甥柳玼之。

translations.literal: When he returned home, his nephew-in-law Liu Can reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Liu Can reproached him on returning home.

sentences.zh: 澳曰：「主上不與宰輔僉議，私慾用我，人必謂我以他歧得之，何以自明！

translations.literal: Ao said, "The sovereign does not consult the chief ministers but privately wishes to use me—people will surely say I gained it by some other path; how can I clear myself!
translations.idiomatic: “Ao said a private appointment would look like favoritism and ruin his name.

sentences.zh: 且爾知時事浸不佳乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, do you not know that affairs grow worse by the day?
translations.idiomatic: He asked whether Liu Can saw how bad times had become.

sentences.zh: 由吾曹貪名位所致耳。」

translations.literal: It is because men like us greedily cling to name and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Men like us, he said, caused the decline by clinging to office."

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以澳為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Ao was made military commissioner of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bingchen: Ao became Heyang military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 玼仲郢之子也。

translations.literal: Can was the son of Liu Zhongying.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can was Liu Zhongying's son.

sentences.zh: 上欲幸華清宮，諫官論之甚切，上為之止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to visit Huaqing Palace; remonstrating officials argued so forcefully that he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Censors talked him out of visiting Huaqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 上樂聞規諫，凡諫官論事、門下封駁，苟合於理，多屈意從之；

translations.literal: The emperor delighted in hearing remonstrance; whenever remonstrating officials spoke or the Gate Bureau sealed and returned memorials, if the reasoning fit he often bent his will to comply;
translations.idiomatic: He often yielded when remonstrance or Gate Bureau objections were sound;

sentences.zh: 得大臣章疏，必焚香盥手而讀之。

translations.literal: when he received chief ministers' memorials he invariably burned incense and washed his hands before reading them.
translations.idiomatic: and he burned incense and washed his hands before reading ministers' papers.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛巳，以門下侍郎、同平章事魏謨同平章事，充西川節度使。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinsi, Vice Director of the Gate Bureau and Co-Equal Chief Minister Wei Mo was made Co-Equal Chief Minister and military commissioner of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, xinsi: Wei Mo went out to Xichuan as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 謨為相，議事於上前，它相或委曲規諷，謨獨正言無所避。

translations.literal: As chief minister Mo discussed policy before the throne; other chancellors might speak indirectly, but Mo alone spoke plainly without evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Mo alone spoke bluntly where other chancellors circled around issues.

sentences.zh: 上每歎曰：「謨綽有祖風，我心重之」。

translations.literal: The emperor often sighed, "Mo has his grandfather's manner in full—I hold him dear."
translations.idiomatic: “The emperor praised Mo's grandfatherly forthrightness.”

sentences.zh: 然竟以剛直為令狐綯所忌而出之。

translations.literal: Yet in the end, because of his rigidity, he was envied by Linghu Tao and sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Tao's jealousy finally drove the upright Mo from court.

sentences.zh: 嶺南溪洞蠻屢為侵盜。

translations.literal: In the Lingnan stream-cave region the Man repeatedly raided and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan cave tribes kept raiding the borders.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬申，以右千牛大將軍宋涯為安南、邕管宣慰使。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renshen, Right Thousand-Bull General Song Ya was made pacification commissioner of Annan and Yong and Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, renshen: Song Ya was sent to pacify Annan.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙巳，以涯為安南經略使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yisi, Ya was made military commissioner of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, yisi: Ya became Annan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 容州軍亂，逐經略使王球。

translations.literal: The Rongzhou army mutinied and expelled military commissioner Wang Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Rongzhou troops mutinied and drove out Wang Qiu.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸巳，以涯為容管經略使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guisi, Ya was made military commissioner of Rongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, guisi: Ya was shifted to Rongguan.

sentences.zh: 甲午，立皇子灌為衛王，澭為廣王。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Princes Guan was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei and Zong as Prince of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiawu: Princes Guan and Zong were enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚子，以兵部侍郎、判度支蕭鄴同平章事，仍判度支。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengzi, Vice Minister of War and acting commissioner of fiscal affairs Xiao Ye was made Co-Equal Chief Minister, still acting in fiscal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, gengzi: Xiao Ye became chief minister while keeping fiscal affairs.

sentences.zh: 教坊祝漢貞，滑稽敏給，上或指物使之口占，摹詠有如宿構，由是寵冠諸優。

translations.literal: Zhu Hanzhen of the Music Office was witty and quick; the emperor might point at an object and have him improvise verses on the spot as if long prepared, and by this he won favor above all performers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hanzhen improvised verses on command and became the favorite performer.

sentences.zh: 一日，在上前抵掌詼諧，頗及外事。

translations.literal: One day before the throne he clapped hands in jest and touched somewhat on outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One day his banter strayed into state affairs.

sentences.zh: 上正色謂之曰：「我畜養爾曹，正供戲笑耳，豈得輒預朝政邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor said sternly, "I keep you people only to supply laughter—how dare you meddle in court government!"
translations.idiomatic: “The emperor warned that performers were for amusement, not politics.”

sentences.zh: 自是疏之。

translations.literal: From then on he kept his distance.
translations.idiomatic: After that he lost favor.

sentences.zh: 會其子坐贓，杖死，流漢貞於天德軍。

translations.literal: Soon his son was convicted of corruption, beaten to death, and Hanzhen was exiled to the Tiande Army.
translations.idiomatic: His son's corruption cost him his life; Hanzhen was exiled north.

sentences.zh: 樂工羅程，善琵琶，自武宗朝已得幸。

translations.literal: Musician Luo Cheng was skilled at the pipa and had enjoyed favor since Emperor Wuzong's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Pipa master Luo Cheng had been favored since Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 上素曉音律，尤有寵。

translations.literal: The emperor was versed in music and favored him especially.
translations.idiomatic: Xuānzong, a music lover, favored him most.

sentences.zh: 程恃恩暴橫，以睚眥殺人，系京兆獄。

translations.literal: Cheng relied on favor and was violent; for a petty grudge he killed a man and was imprisoned by the capital prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng murdered over a slight and landed in the capital jail.

sentences.zh: 諸樂工欲為之請，因上幸後苑奏樂，乃設虛坐，置琵琶，而羅拜於庭，且泣。

translations.literal: The musicians wished to plead for him; when the emperor visited the rear park for music they set an empty seat with a pipa and all bowed in the courtyard, weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians set out an empty seat and wept in the rear park to beg his life.

sentences.zh: 上問其故，對曰：「羅程負陛下，萬死，然臣等惜其天下絕藝，不復得奉宴游矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; they replied, "Luo Cheng has wronged Your Majesty and deserves ten thousand deaths, yet we mourn that his peerless art under heaven will never again grace Your banquets!"
translations.idiomatic: “They said Cheng deserved death but his art would be lost forever.”

sentences.zh: 上曰：「汝曹所惜者羅程藝，朕所惜者高祖、太宗法。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What you cherish is Luo Cheng's art; what I cherish is the law of Emperors Gaozu and Taizong."
translations.idiomatic: “The emperor said they valued art; he valued Taizong's law.”

sentences.zh: 竟杖殺之。

translations.literal: In the end he was beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was flogged to death anyway.

sentences.zh: 八月，成德節度使王紹鼎薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Chengde military commissioner Wang Shaoding died.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: Wang Shaoding of Chengde died.

sentences.zh: 紹鼎沉湎無度，好登樓彈射人以為樂，眾欲逐之。

translations.literal: Shaoding was sunk in dissipation without limit and loved to climb towers and shoot people for amusement; the troops wished to drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoding shot people from towers for sport until the army wanted him gone.

sentences.zh: 會病薨，軍中立其弟節度副命名紹懿。

translations.literal: When he fell ill and died, the army installed his younger brother, deputy commissioner Wang Shaoyi, by name.
translations.idiomatic: He died; the troops made his brother Shaoyi commissioner.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以紹懿為成德留後。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Shaoyi was made acting commissioner of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyin: Shaoyi became Chengde acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛酉，以太子太師盧鈞同平章事，充山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinyou, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Lu Jun was made Co-Equal Chief Minister and military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, xinyou: Lu Jun went to Shannan West as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己巳，以秦成防禦使李承勳為涇原節度使。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jisi, Qincheng defense commissioner Li Chengxun was made military commissioner of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, jisi: Li Chengxun took Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 承勳，光弼之孫也。

translations.literal: Chengxun was the grandson of Li Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: He was Li Guangbi's grandson.

sentences.zh: 先是，吐蕃酉長尚延心以河、渭二州部落來降，拜武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Tibetan chieftain Shang Yanxin had come over with the He and Wei prefecture tribes and was appointed General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan chief Shang Yanxin had surrendered with He and Wei tribes.

sentences.zh: 承勳利其羊馬之富，誘之入鳳林關，居秦州之西。

translations.literal: Chengxun coveted the wealth of their sheep and horses and lured them through Fenglin Pass to settle west of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun lured them through Fenglin Pass for their herds.

sentences.zh: 承勳與諸將謀執延心，誣雲謀叛，盡掠其財，徙其眾於荒遠。

translations.literal: Chengxun and the generals plotted to seize Yanxin, falsely charged him with plotting rebellion, plundered all his wealth, and moved his people to remote wastes.
translations.idiomatic: They framed Yanxin for rebellion and looted his people.

sentences.zh: 延心知之，因承勳軍宴，坐中謂承勳曰：「河、渭二州，土曠人稀，因以饑疫。

translations.literal: Yanxin knew it; at Chengxun's army feast he said from his seat, "The He and Wei region is broad land with few people, and so famine and pestilence follow.
translations.idiomatic: “At a feast Yanxin warned that He and Wei were empty and plague-ridden.

sentences.zh: 唐人多內徙三川，吐蕃皆遠遁於疊宕之西，二千里間，寂無人煙。

translations.literal: Many Tang people have moved inward to the Three Rivers; the Tibetans have all fled far west beyond Die and Dang—for two thousand li there is no human smoke.
translations.idiomatic: Tang settlers filled the Three Rivers while Tibetans fled two thousand li west.

sentences.zh: 延心欲入見天子，請盡帥部眾分徙內地，為唐百姓，使西邊永無揚塵之警，其功亦不愧於張義潮矣。」

translations.literal: Yanxin wished to enter court and beg to lead all his tribes inland to become Tang commoners, so that the western border would never again see rising dust of alarm—his merit would not shame Zhang Yichao."
translations.idiomatic: He offered to resettle his tribes as Tang subjects like Zhang Yichao had."

sentences.zh: 承勳欲自有其功，猶豫未許。

translations.literal: Chengxun wished to keep the credit himself and hesitated, not consenting.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun hesitated, wanting the credit himself.

sentences.zh: 延心復曰：「延心既入朝，落部內徙，但惜秦州無所復恃耳。」

translations.literal: Yanxin said again, "Once Yanxin enters court and his remaining tribes move inward, I only fear Qin Prefecture will have nothing left to rely on."
translations.idiomatic: “Yanxin said Qinzhou would be helpless once his people moved in.”

sentences.zh: 承勳與諸將相顧默然。

translations.literal: Chengxun and the generals looked at one another in silence.
translations.idiomatic: The generals fell silent.

sentences.zh: 明日，諸將言於承勳曰：「明公首開營田，置使府，擁萬兵，仰給度支，將士無戰守之勞，有耕市之利。

translations.literal: The next day the generals said to Chengxun, "Your Excellency first opened military farms and established a commissioner's headquarters, holding ten thousand troops supplied by the fiscal circuit—the soldiers have no war or garrison labor but gain from farming and trade.
translations.idiomatic: “His officers said his command thrived on frontier farms and fiscal support.

sentences.zh: 若從延心之謀，則西陲無事，朝廷必罷使府，省戍兵，還以秦州隸鳳翔，吾屬無所復望矣。」

translations.literal: If Yanxin's plan is followed, the western border will be quiet, the court will surely abolish the commissioner's post, reduce garrison troops, and return Qin Prefecture to Fengxiang—we will have nothing more to hope for."
translations.idiomatic: They warned that peace would abolish their lucrative command."

sentences.zh: 承勳以為然，即奏延心為河、渭都游奕使，使統其眾居之。

translations.literal: Chengxun thought it so and at once memorialized making Yanxin roaming inspector of He and Wei, to command his people in residence there.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun kept Yanxin on the border as He-Wei inspector instead.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同平章事鄭朗以疾辭位。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal Chief Minister Zheng Lang resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Lang resigned ill.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以朗為太子太師。

translations.literal: On renshen, Lang was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Renshen: Lang became grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 上晚節頗好神仙，遣中使迎道士軒轅集於羅浮山。

translations.literal: In his later years the emperor greatly favored immortals and sent palace envoys to welcome the Daoist Xuanyuan Ji from Mount Luofu.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he sent for the Daoist Xuanyuan Ji on Mount Luofu.

sentences.zh: 王端章冊立回鶻可汗，道為黑車子所塞，不至而還。

translations.literal: Wang Duanzhang, enfeoffing the Uyghur qaghan, was blocked on the road by the Qara Khitai and returned without arriving.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duanzhang never reached the Uyghurs; Qara Khitai blocked the road.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，貶端章賀州司馬。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Duanzhang was demoted to vice-governor of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xinmao: Duanzhang was demoted to Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬寅，以成德軍留後王紹懿為節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on renyin, acting commissioner of the Chengde army Wang Shaoyi was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, renyin: Shaoyi became full Chengde commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十二月，蕭鄴罷判度支。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xiao Ye ceased acting in fiscal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month: Xiao Ye left fiscal affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣宗元聖至明成武獻文睿智章仁神聰懿道大孝皇帝下大中十二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuānzong—below; twelfth year of the Dazhong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuānzong—below; Dazhong year twelve (

sentences.zh: 戌寅，公元八五八年）

translations.literal: wuyin, corresponding to 858 CE)
translations.idiomatic: wuyin, 858 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，以康王傅、分司王式為安南都護、經略使。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Wang Shi, tutor to the Prince of Kang and eastern capital official, was made protector-general and military commissioner of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, first month: Wang Shi became Annan protector and commissioner.

sentences.zh: 式有才略，至交趾，樹芀木為柵，可支數十年。

translations.literal: Shi was resourceful; reaching Jiaozhi, he built palisades of ngau wood that could stand for decades.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiaozhi he built ngau-wood palisades meant to last decades.

sentences.zh: 深塹其外，洩城中水，塹外植竹，寇不能冒。

translations.literal: He dug a deep moat outside, drained the city water into it, and planted bamboo beyond the moat so raiders could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: A moat, drained city water, and bamboo blocked raiders.

sentences.zh: 選教士卒甚銳。

translations.literal: He selected and trained troops with great sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled an elite garrison.

sentences.zh: 頃之，南蠻大至，屯錦田步，去交趾半日程。

translations.literal: Before long the southern Man came in force, encamped at Jintian Ford half a day's march from Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Southern tribes camped half a day from Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 式意思安閒，遣譯逾之，中其要害，蠻一夕引去，遣人謝曰：「我自執叛獠耳，非為寇也。」

translations.literal: Shi remained calm; he sent interpreters across to strike their vital point, and the Man withdrew in one night and sent word of apology, saying, "We came only to seize rebellious liao ourselves, not as invaders."
translations.idiomatic: “Shi's envoys hit their weak point; the Man withdrew claiming they sought rebels only.”

sentences.zh: 安南都校羅行恭，久專府政，麾下精兵二千，都護中軍才羸兵數百。

translations.literal: Colonel Luo Xinggong of Annan had long monopolized prefectural government; under him were two thousand crack troops while the protector's central army had only a few hundred weak soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Luo Xinggong ruled Annan with two thousand veterans against a weak protector guard.

sentences.zh: 式至，杖其背，黜於邊徼。

translations.literal: When Shi arrived, he flogged Xinggong's back and banished him to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Shi flogged and exiled Xinggong.

sentences.zh: 初，戶部侍郎、判度支劉瑑為翰林學士，上器重之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Vice Minister of Revenue and acting commissioner of fiscal affairs Liu Zhuan had been a Hanlin academician and the emperor valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhuan, once Hanlin and fiscal vice minister, had been highly valued.

sentences.zh: 時為河東節度使。

translations.literal: He was then military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was then at Hedong.

sentences.zh: 手詔征入朝，瑑奏發河東，外人始知之。

translations.literal: An imperial autograph summoned him to court; when Zhuan memorialized his departure from Hedong, outsiders first learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: A secret summons reached him only when he left Hedong.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以瑑同平章事。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Zhuan was made Co-Equal Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwu: Liu Zhuan became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 瑑，仁軌之五世孫也。

translations.literal: Zhuan was a descendant in the fifth generation of Liu Rengui.
translations.idiomatic: He was Liu Rengui's fifth-generation descendant.

sentences.zh: 瑑與崔慎由議政於上前，慎由曰：「惟當甄別品流，上酬萬一。」

translations.literal: Zhuan and Cui Shenyou discussed policy before the throne; Shenyou said, "One need only distinguish grades of pedigree to repay the myriad in one part."
translations.idiomatic: “Shenyou said offices should reward pedigree.”

sentences.zh: 彖曰：「昔王夷甫祖尚浮華，妄分流品，致中原丘虛。

translations.literal: Zhuan said, "In the past Wang Yifu's clan favored empty show and recklessly divided grades of pedigree, bringing the Central Plains to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: “Zhuan cited Wang Yifu's pedigree obsession that ruined the north.

sentences.zh: 今盛明之朝，當循名責實，使百官各稱其職；

translations.literal: In this age of great brilliance one should follow names and demand realities, so that all officials fulfill their duties;
translations.idiomatic: He urged merit over birth in a brilliant age.

sentences.zh: 而遽以品流為先，臣未知致理之日。」

translations.literal: yet to put pedigree first—I do not yet see the day of good order."
translations.idiomatic: Putting pedigree first, he said, would never bring order."

sentences.zh: 慎由無以對。

translations.literal: Shenyou had no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyou was silent.

sentences.zh: 軒轅集至長安，上召入禁中，問曰：「長生可學乎？」

translations.literal: When Xuanyuan Ji reached Chang'an, the emperor summoned him to the inner palace and asked, "Can long life be learned?"
translations.idiomatic: “The emperor asked Xuanyuan Ji whether immortality could be learned.”

sentences.zh: 對曰：「王者屏欲而崇德，則自然受天遐福，何處更求長生？」

translations.literal: He replied, "A king who screens desires and honors virtue naturally receives Heaven's far blessing—where else would you seek long life?"
translations.idiomatic: “Ji said virtue, not elixirs, brings long life.”

sentences.zh: 留數月，堅求還山，乃遣之。

translations.literal: After several months he firmly begged to return to the mountains and was sent away.
translations.idiomatic: After months he returned to the mountains.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲子朔，罷公卿朝拜光陵及忌日行香，悉移宮人於諸陵。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the jiazi new moon, court nobles' worship at Emperor Guang's tomb and anniversary incense offerings were abolished; all palace women were moved to the various tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, jiazi: Guang tomb rites ended; palace women sent to tombs.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以中書侍郎、同平章事崔慎由為東川節度使。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal Chief Minister Cui Shenyou was made military commissioner of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchen: Cui Shenyou went to Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 上欲御樓肆赦，令狐綯曰：「御樓所費甚廣，事須有名，且赦不可數。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to ascend the tower for a great amnesty; Linghu Tao said, "The tower ceremony costs very much; there must be a name for it, and amnesties must not be frequent."
translations.idiomatic: “Linghu Tao blocked a costly tower amnesty.”

sentences.zh: 上不悅，曰：「遣朕於何得名！」

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and said, "Then where am I to get a name!"
translations.idiomatic: “The emperor snapped that Tao gave him no occasion for one.”

sentences.zh: 慎由曰：「陛下未建儲宮，四海屬望。

translations.literal: Shenyou said, "Your Majesty has not yet established an heir—the realm looks to it.
translations.idiomatic: “Shenyou said naming an heir would justify even suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 若舉此禮，雖郊祀亦可，況於御樓！」

translations.literal: If you perform this rite, even suburban sacrifice would do—how much more a tower!"
translations.idiomatic: A tower amnesty was trivial compared with investiture, he said."

sentences.zh: 時上餌方士藥，已覺躁渴，而外人未知，疑忌方深，聞之，俯首不復言。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was taking alchemists' drugs and already felt thirst and agitation, but outsiders did not know; his suspicion ran deep, and hearing this he bowed his head and spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: The drug-sick emperor fell silent at the heir hint.

sentences.zh: 旬日，慎由罷相。

translations.literal: Within ten days Shenyou was removed as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Shenyou left the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 勃海王彝震卒。

translations.literal: King Yizhen of Bohai died.
translations.idiomatic: Bohai King Yizhen died.

sentences.zh: 癸未，立其弟虔晃為勃海王。

translations.literal: On guiwei, his younger brother Qianhuang was installed as King of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Guiwei: Qianhuang became Bohai king.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，以右街使、附馬都尉劉異為邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Right Street Commissioner and imperial son-in-law Liu Yi was made military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month: Liu Yi took Binning.

sentences.zh: 異尚安平公主，上妹也。

translations.literal: Yi had married Princess Anping, the emperor's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: He had married the emperor's sister.

sentences.zh: 庚子，嶺南都將王令寰作亂，囚節度使楊發。

translations.literal: On gengzi, a southern Lingnan garrison officer, Wang Linghuan, rebelled and imprisoned military commissioner Yang Fa.
translations.idiomatic: Gengzi: Wang Linghuan imprisoned Yang Fa.

sentences.zh: 發，蘇州人也。

translations.literal: Fa was a man of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fa came from Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以兵部侍郎、鹽鐵轉運使夏侯孜同平章事。

translations.literal: On wushen, Vice Minister of War and salt and iron transport commissioner Xiahou Zi was made Co-Equal Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wushen: Xiahou Zi entered the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙寅，工部尚書、同平章事劉瑑薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on bingyin, Minister of Works and Co-Equal Chief Minister Liu Zhuan died.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, bingyin: Liu Zhuan died.

sentences.zh: 瑑病篤，猶手疏論事，上皆惜之。

translations.literal: Though gravely ill, Zhuan still wrote memorials by hand on policy; the emperor mourned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, Zhuan still memorialized; the emperor mourned each paper.

sentences.zh: 以右金吾大將軍李燧為嶺南節度使，已命中使賜之節，給事中蕭倣封還制書。

translations.literal: Right Golden Guard General Li Sui was made military commissioner of Lingnan; the commission had been issued and a palace envoy sent to bestow the tally, but Remonstrance Officer Xiao Fang sealed and returned the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sui's Lingnan appointment was blocked when Xiao Fang returned the edict.

sentences.zh: 上方奏樂，不暇別召中使，使優人追之，節及燧門而返。

translations.literal: The emperor was listening to music and had no time to summon another envoy separately; he had a performer pursue him—the tally reached Li Sui's gate and returned.
translations.idiomatic: A musician-chaser overtook the envoy at Li Sui's gate and brought the tally back.

sentences.zh: 倣，俛之從父弟也。

translations.literal: Fang was a cousin of Xiao Ni.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fang was Xiao Ni's cousin.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以涇原節度使李承勳為嶺南節度使，發鄰道兵討亂者，平之。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Jingyuan military commissioner Li Chengxun was made military commissioner of Lingnan; he raised neighboring-circuit troops to suppress the rebels and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Xinsi: Li Chengxun pacified Lingnan with neighbor troops.

sentences.zh: 是日，湖南軍亂，都將石載順等逐觀察使韓悰，殺都押牙王桂直。

translations.literal: That same day the Hunan army mutinied; garrison commander Shi Zaishun and others expelled observation commissioner Han Cong and killed chief adjutant Wang Guizhi.
translations.idiomatic: The same day Hunan troops expelled Han Cong and killed Wang Guizhi.

sentences.zh: 琮待將士不以禮，故及於難。

translations.literal: Cong had not treated the officers with courtesy, and so met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Han Cong's discourtesy toward officers caused the mutiny.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙申，江西軍亂，都將毛鶴逐觀察使鄭憲。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingshen, the Jiangxi army mutinied; garrison commander Mao He expelled observation commissioner Zheng Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, bingshen: Mao He drove out Zheng Xian in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 初，安南都護李涿為政貪暴，強市蠻中馬牛，一頭止與鹽一鬥。

translations.literal: Earlier, protector-general of Annan Li Zhuo had governed with greed and violence, forcibly buying Man horses and cattle at one picul of salt per head.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhuo had cheated tribes for horses at a picul of salt each.

sentences.zh: 又殺蠻酋杜存誠。

translations.literal: He also killed the Man chief Du Cuncheng.
translations.idiomatic: He murdered chief Du Cuncheng.

sentences.zh: 群蠻怨怒，導南詔侵盜邊境。

translations.literal: The tribes resented and hated him and guided Nanzhao to raid the border.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes guided Nanzhao raids in revenge.

sentences.zh: 峰州有林西原，舊有防冬兵六千，其旁七綰洞蠻，其酋長曰李由獨，常助中國戍守，輸租賦。

translations.literal: West of Lin in Feng Prefecture was the old winter-garrison of six thousand; beside it were seven cave tribes of the Man, whose chieftain Li Youdu had long helped China garrison and paid rents and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Li Youdu's seven caves had long aided Fengzhou garrisons.

sentences.zh: 知峰州者言於涿，請罷戍兵，專委由獨防遏。

translations.literal: Whoever knew Feng Prefecture told Zhuo and asked to withdraw the garrison and entrust defense entirely to Youdu.
translations.idiomatic: Officials urged Zhuo to rely on Youdu and pull the garrison.

sentences.zh: 於是由獨勢孤，不能自立，南詔拓東節度使以書誘之，以甥妻其子，補拓東押牙，由獨遂帥其眾臣於南詔。

translations.literal: Thus Youdu was isolated and could not stand alone; the Nanzhao Tuodong military commissioner wrote to entice him, gave his nephew in marriage to Youdu's son, and appointed him Tuodong adjutant—Youdu then led his people to submit to Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Isolated, Youdu submitted to Nanzhao through marriage and rank.

sentences.zh: 自是安南始有蠻患。

translations.literal: From this Annan first had Man troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Annan's tribal troubles began here.

sentences.zh: 是月，蠻寇安南。

translations.literal: That month the Man raided Annan.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Man attacked Annan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙寅，宣州都將康全泰作亂，逐觀察使鄭薰。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingyin, Xu Prefecture garrison commander Kang Quantai rebelled and expelled observation commissioner Zheng Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, bingyin: Kang Quantai expelled Zheng Xun.

sentences.zh: 薰奔揚州。

translations.literal: Xun fled to Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fled to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，右補闕內供奉張潛上疏，以為：「籓府代移之際，皆奏倉庫蓄積之數，以羨餘多為課績，朝廷亦因而甄獎。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Remonstrance Officer and inner attendant Zhang Qian submitted a memorial holding that, "When frontier prefectures change hands, all report storehouse accumulations, taking surplus as achievement, and the court also rewards selection thereby.
translations.idiomatic: “Zhang Qian warned that reporting warehouse surpluses encouraged abuse.

sentences.zh: 竊惟籓府財賦，所出有常，苟非賦斂過差，及停廢將士，減削衣糧，則羨餘何從而致！

translations.literal: I consider that frontier wealth has fixed sources; unless levies exceed measure, or troops are disbanded and clothing and grain cut, whence comes surplus!
translations.idiomatic: Surplus, he said, could only come from extortion or starving soldiers.

sentences.zh: 比來南方諸鎮數有不寧，皆此故也。

translations.literal: Recently several southern circuits have been unsettled—all for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Southern unrest, he argued, came from false surpluses.

sentences.zh: 一朝有變，所蓄之財悉遭剽掠。

translations.literal: Once trouble arises, stored wealth is all plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Stored wealth would be looted in any revolt.

sentences.zh: 又發兵致討，費用百倍，然則朝廷竟有何利！

translations.literal: Again troops are sent to punish—cost a hundredfold; what profit does the court finally have!
translations.idiomatic: Punitive campaigns cost far more than any gain.

sentences.zh: 乞自今籓府長吏，不增賦斂，不減糧賜，獨節游宴，省浮費，能致羨餘者，然後賞之。」

translations.literal: I beg that from now frontier chief officials neither increase levies nor reduce grain and clothing, but only cut banquets and floating expense; only those who can produce real surplus should then be rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to reward only honest surplus after cutting waste."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 容管奏都虞候來正謀叛，經略使宋涯捕斬之。

translations.literal: Rongguan reported that chief adjutant Lai Zheng plotted rebellion; military commissioner Song Ya seized and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ya executed the alleged rebel Lai Zheng at Rongguan.

sentences.zh: 初，忠武軍精兵皆以黃冒首，號黃頭軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, the crack troops of the Zhongwu army all wore yellow on their heads and were called the Yellow Head Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu's elite wore yellow headcloths—the Yellow Head Army.

sentences.zh: 李承勳以百人定嶺南，宋涯使麾下效其服裝，亦定容州。

translations.literal: Li Chengxun with a hundred men pacified Lingnan; Song Ya had his subordinates copy their dress and also pacified Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun's hundred Yellow Heads pacified Lingnan; Song Ya copied them at Rong.

sentences.zh: 安南有惡民，屢為亂，聞之，驚曰：「黃頭軍度海來襲我矣！」

translations.literal: In Annan there were wicked commoners who repeatedly made trouble; hearing this, they cried in alarm, "The Yellow Head Army has crossed the sea to strike us!"
translations.idiomatic: In Annan, violent locals repeatedly made trouble. When they heard of this, they panicked and cried, "The Yellow Head Army has crossed the sea to attack us!"

sentences.zh: 相與夜圍交趾城，鼓噪：「願送都護北歸，我須此城御黃頭軍。」

translations.literal: Together they surrounded Jiaozhi by night, shouting, "Send the protector north—we need this city against the Yellow Head Army."
translations.idiomatic: That night they surrounded Jiaozhi together, shouting, "Send the Protector north. We need this city to hold off the Yellow Head Army."

sentences.zh: 王式方食，或勸出避之。

translations.literal: Wang Shi was at his meal when some urged him to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Wang Shi to flee during the siege.

sentences.zh: 式曰：「吾足一動，則城潰矣。」

translations.literal: Shi said, "If I move one foot, the city will collapse."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "If I move so much as one foot, the city will collapse."

sentences.zh: 徐食畢，擐甲，率左右登城，建大將旗，坐而責之，敵者反走。

translations.literal: He finished eating at leisure, donned armor, led his attendants up the wall, raised the great general's banner, sat, and rebuked them—the enemy turned and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He finished dinner, mounted the wall, and stared them down.

sentences.zh: 明日，悉捕誅之。

translations.literal: The next day he seized and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he executed every rebel.

sentences.zh: 有杜守澄者，自齊、梁以來擁眾據溪洞，不可制。

translations.literal: There was one Du Shoucheng who since Qi and Liang had held the stream caves with troops and could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shoucheng had ruled cave lands since the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 式離間其親黨，守澄走死。

translations.literal: Shi set his kin against one another; Shoucheng fled and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shi split his faction until Shoucheng died fleeing.

sentences.zh: 安南饑亂相繼，六年無上供，軍中犒賞。

translations.literal: Annan had hunger and turmoil in succession; for six years there was no tribute upstream, nor army rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Six years passed without tribute or troop rewards.

sentences.zh: 式始修貢賦，饗將士。

translations.literal: When Shi began restoring tribute and tax deliveries, he feasted the officers.
translations.idiomatic: Shi restored tribute and feasted the army.

sentences.zh: 占城、真臘皆復通使。

translations.literal: Champa and Zhenla both resumed sending envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Champa and Zhenla reopened relations.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使崔鉉奏已出兵討宣州賊。

translations.literal: Huainan military commissioner Cui Xuan memorialized that he had already sent troops to attack the Xu Prefecture rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan reported troops sent against Xu rebels.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲午，以鉉兼宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiawu, Xuan was concurrently made observation commissioner of Xuan and She.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, jiawu: Cui Xuan also took Xu-She.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以宋州刺史溫璋為宣州團練使。

translations.literal: On jihai, Song Prefecture prefect Wen Zhang was made Xu Prefecture training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jihai: Wen Zhang became Xu training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 璋，造之子也。

translations.literal: Zhang was the son of Wen Zao.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhang was Wen Zao's son.

sentences.zh: 河南、北、淮南大水，徐、泗水深五丈，漂沒數萬家。

translations.literal: Great floods struck Henan, Hebei, and Huainan; the Xu and Si rivers were five zhang deep and swept away tens of thousands of households.
translations.idiomatic: Great floods struck Henan, Hebei, and Huainan; the Xu and Si rivers rose five zhang deep and swept away tens of thousands of households.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，建州刺史於延陵入辭，上曰：「建州去京師幾何？」

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Jian Prefecture prefect Yu Yanling came to take leave; the emperor said, "How far is Jian Prefecture from the capital?"
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Jian Prefecture prefect Yu Yanling came to take leave. The emperor asked, "How far is Jian Prefecture from the capital?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「八千里。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Eight thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Eight thousand li."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿到彼為政善惡，朕皆知之，勿謂其遠。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Whether your governance there is good or bad, I know it all—do not think it far.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Whether your governance there is good or bad, I will know it all. Do not think it far away.

sentences.zh: 此階前則萬里也，卿知之乎？」

translations.literal: Before these steps it is ten thousand li—do you understand?"
translations.idiomatic: From these palace steps it is ten thousand li. Do you understand?"

sentences.zh: 延陵悸懾失緒，上撫而遣之。

translations.literal: Yanling was startled and lost composure; the emperor comforted him and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Yanling was comforted and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 到官，竟以不職貶復州司馬。

translations.literal: Once in office, he was in the end demoted to vice-governor of Fu Prefecture for incompetence.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted for incompetence once he took office.

sentences.zh: 令狐綯擬李遠杭州刺史，上曰：「吾聞遠詩云：『長日惟消一局棋』，安能理人！」

translations.literal: Linghu Tao proposed Li Yuan as Hang Prefecture prefect; the emperor said, "I have heard Yuan's verse, 'Long days are spent only on a chess game'—how can he govern people!"
translations.idiomatic: ‘The emperor rejected Li Yuan for a poem about playing chess all day.’

sentences.zh: 綯曰：「詩人托此為高興耳，未必實然。」

translations.literal: Tao said, "Poets use that for lofty mood—it need not be real."
translations.idiomatic: “Tao said poets exaggerate.”

sentences.zh: 上曰：「且令往試觀之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Let him go try and we shall see."
translations.idiomatic: “The emperor said to try him anyway.”

sentences.zh: 上詔刺史毋得外徙，必令至京師，面察其能否，然後除之。

translations.literal: The emperor decreed that prefects must not take outside appointments but must come to the capital so he could examine their ability face to face before appointing them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered all prefects to the capital for face-to-face vetting.

sentences.zh: 令狐綯嘗徙其故人為鄰州刺史，便道之官。

translations.literal: Linghu Tao once transferred an old friend to a neighboring prefecture and let him take office by the direct route.
translations.idiomatic: Tao sent a friend to a neighbor prefecture by shortcut.

sentences.zh: 上見其謝上表，以問綯，對曰：「以其道近，省送迎耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor saw his memorial of thanks and questioned Tao, who replied, "Because the route was near, to save the trouble of escort and reception."
translations.idiomatic: “Tao said he spared escorts because the post was nearby.”

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕以刺史多非其人，為百姓害，故欲一一見之，訪問其所施設，知其優劣以行黜陟。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Because so many prefects are unfit and harm the people, I wished to see each one, inquire what he has done, know his merit and fault, and promote or demote accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: “The emperor said he wanted to interview every prefect because most were harmful.

sentences.zh: 而詔命既行，直廢格不用，宰相可畏有權！」

translations.literal: Yet the edict had already gone forth and was simply set aside unused—the chief minister's power is fearsome!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tao had voided the edict—the chancellor's power terrified him."

sentences.zh: 時方寒，綯汗透重裘。

translations.literal: It was just then cold, yet Tao's sweat soaked through his heavy fur.
translations.idiomatic: In the cold Tao sweated through his furs.

sentences.zh: 上臨朝，接對群臣如賓客，雖左右近習，未嘗見其有惰容。

translations.literal: When the emperor held court he received the ministers like guests; even those close at hand never saw a lazy look on his face.
translations.idiomatic: At court he treated ministers as guests and never looked idle.

sentences.zh: 每宰相奏事，旁無一人立者，威嚴不可仰視。

translations.literal: Whenever the chief ministers reported, no one stood beside them—the majesty could not be looked up to.
translations.idiomatic: No attendant stood near when chancellors reported; his majesty was overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 奏事畢，忽怡然曰：「可以閒語矣。」

translations.literal: When the report was finished he would suddenly say pleasantly, "We may speak at ease now."
translations.idiomatic: Then he would relax: "We may speak at ease."

sentences.zh: 因問閭閻細事，或談宮中游宴，無所不至。

translations.literal: He would ask about neighborhood trifles or talk of palace feasts—nothing was beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: He chatted about streets or palace revels.

sentences.zh: 一刻許，復整容曰：「卿輩善為之，朕常恐卿輩負朕，後日不復得再相見。」

translations.literal: After about a quarter of an hour he would compose his face again and say, "You must do well; I always fear you will fail me—we may not meet again."
translations.idiomatic: “Then he turned grave, warning they might never meet again.”

sentences.zh: 乃起入宮。

translations.literal: He would rise and enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: And he returned to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 令狐綯謂人曰：「吾十年秉政，最承恩遇；

translations.literal: Linghu Tao told others, "I have held power ten years and received the greatest grace;
translations.idiomatic: “Linghu Tao said ten years in power brought the greatest favor—

sentences.zh: 然每延英奏事，未嘗不汗沾衣也！」

translations.literal: yet every Yanying report never failed to soak my robe with sweat!"
translations.idiomatic: yet every Yanying session soaked his robe with sweat."

sentences.zh: 初，山南東道節度使徐商，以封疆險闊，素多盜賊，選精兵數百人別置營訓練，號捕盜將。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shannan East Circuit military commissioner Xu Shang, because the territory was broad and dangerous and had always had many bandits, chose several hundred crack troops, set up a separate camp to train them, and called them the Bandit-Catching Generals.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shang trained Bandit-Catching Generals for his rugged circuit.

sentences.zh: 及湖南逐帥，詔商討之。

translations.literal: When Hunan drove out its commissioner, an edict ordered Shang to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hunan mutinied, Shang was ordered to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 南遣捕盜將二百人討平之。

translations.literal: Shang sent two hundred Bandit-Catching Generals south and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred of them pacified Hunan.

sentences.zh: 崔鉉奏克宣州，斬康全泰及其黨四百餘人。

translations.literal: Cui Xuan memorialized the capture of Xu Prefecture and the beheading of Kang Quantai and more than four hundred of his party.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan reported Xu taken and four hundred rebels executed.

sentences.zh: 上以光祿卿韋宙父丹有惠政於江西，以宙為江西觀察使，發鄰道兵以討毛鶴。

translations.literal: Because Director of the Imperial Banquets Wei Zhou's father Dan had benevolent government in Jiangxi, the emperor made Zhou observation commissioner of Jiangxi and raised neighboring-circuit troops to attack Mao He.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhou was sent to Jiangxi for his father's reputation and to fight Mao He.

sentences.zh: 崔鉉以宣州已平，辭宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: Cui Xuan, since Xu Prefecture was pacified, resigned the Xuan-She observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan resigned Xuan-She once Xu was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊寅，以溫璋為宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuyin, Wen Zhang was made observation commissioner of Xuan and She.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, wuyin: Wen Zhang took Xuan-She.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍部、判戶部蔣伸從容言於上曰：「近日官頗易得，人思僥倖。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War and acting commissioner of revenue Jiang Shen said gently to the emperor, "Recently office has been rather easy to obtain—people think of luck."
translations.idiomatic: “Jiang Shen warned that offices came too easily and bred opportunism.”

sentences.zh: 上驚曰：「如此，則亂矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor started and said, "If so, there will be chaos!"
translations.idiomatic: “The emperor cried that such ease would bring chaos.”

sentences.zh: 對曰：「亂則未亂，但僥倖者多，亂亦非難。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Chaos has not come yet, but with so many opportunists, chaos is not hard."
translations.idiomatic: “Jiang Shen said chaos was not far off.”

sentences.zh: 上稱歎再三。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed praise again and again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed his approval repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 伸三起，上三留之，曰：「異日不復得獨對卿矣。」

translations.literal: Shen rose three times; the emperor detained him three times and said, "Another day I may not speak with you alone again."
translations.idiomatic: “Three times Shen rose; three times the emperor kept him, saying they might not meet alone again.”

sentences.zh: 伸不諭。

translations.literal: Shen did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Shen did not understand.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲寅，以伸同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiayin, Shen was made Co-Equal Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, jiayin: Jiang Shen became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 韋宙奏克洪州，斬毛鶴及其黨五百餘人。

translations.literal: Wei Zhou memorialized the capture of Hong Prefecture and the beheading of Mao He and more than five hundred of his party.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhou reported Hongzhou taken and five hundred rebels killed.

sentences.zh: 宙過襄州，徐商遣都將韓季友帥捕盜將從行。

translations.literal: When Zhou passed Xiang Prefecture, Xu Shang sent chief commander Han Jiyou to lead the Bandit-Catching Generals to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang, Xu Shang lent Han Jiyou's Bandit-Catchers to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 宙至江州，季友請夜帥其眾自陸道間行，比明，至洪州，州人不知，即日討平之，宙奏留捕盜將二百人於江西，以季友為都虞候。

translations.literal: When Zhou reached Jiang Prefecture, Jiyou asked to lead his men by land by night on a hidden route; by dawn they reached Hong Prefecture before the people knew, and that day pacified it; Zhou memorialized leaving two hundred Bandit-Catching Generals in Jiangxi and made Jiyou chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: They marched by night, seized Hongzhou at dawn, and left two hundred Bandit-Catchers in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 宣宗元聖至明成武獻文睿智章仁神聰懿道大孝皇帝下大中十三年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuānzong—below; thirteenth year of the Dazhong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuānzong—below; Dazhong year thirteen (

sentences.zh: 己卯，公元八五九年）

translations.literal: jimao, corresponding to 859 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jimao, 859 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊午朔，赦天下。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the wuwu new moon, an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, first month, wuwu: general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 三月，割河東雲、蔚、朔三州隸大同軍。

translations.literal: In the third month, Yun, Wei, and Shuo prefectures of Hedong were detached to the Datong army.
translations.idiomatic: Third month: three Hedong prefectures went to Datong.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛卯，以校書郎于琮為左拾遺內供奉。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinmao, proofreader Yu Cong was made Left Remonstrance and inner attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, xinmao: Yu Cong became left remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 初，上欲以悰尚永福公主，既而中寢。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had wished to marry Cong to Princess Yongfu; he then set the matter aside.
translations.idiomatic: He had planned to marry Cong to Princess Yongfu, then dropped it.

sentences.zh: 宰相請其故，上曰：「朕近與此女子會食，對朕輒折匕箸。

translations.literal: The chief ministers asked the reason; the emperor said, "Recently I dined with this girl; facing me she kept breaking her chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: “He said she broke chopsticks at dinner before him.

sentences.zh: 性情如是，豈可為士大夫妻！」

translations.literal: Her nature is such—how could she be a scholar-official's wife!"
translations.idiomatic: Such temper, he said, unfit her for a minister's household."

sentences.zh: 乃更命悰尚廣德公主。

translations.literal: He then ordered Cong married to Princess Guangde instead.
translations.idiomatic: He married Cong to Princess Guangde instead.

sentences.zh: 二公主皆上女。

translations.literal: Both princesses were the emperor's daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Both were imperial daughters.

sentences.zh: 琮，敖之子也。

translations.literal: Cong was the son of Yu Ao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Cong was Yu Ao's son.

sentences.zh: 武寧節度使康季榮不恤士卒，士卒噪而逐之。

translations.literal: Wuning military commissioner Kang Jirong did not care for the soldiers; the soldiers clamored and drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Jirong neglected troops and was expelled.

sentences.zh: 上以左金吾大將軍田牟嘗鎮徐州，有能名，復以為武寧節度使，一方遂安。

translations.literal: Because Left Golden Guard General Tian Mou had once governed Xuzhou and had a reputation for ability, he was again made Wuning military commissioner and the region was soon settled.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Mou, once popular at Xuzhou, restored order at Wuning.

sentences.zh: 貶季榮於嶺南。

translations.literal: Jirong was demoted to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Jirong was banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸巳，封憲宗子惕為彭王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guisi, Emperor Xianzong's son Ti was enfeoffed as Prince of Peng.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, guisi: Prince Ti of Peng was enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 初，上長子鄆王溫，無寵，居十六宅，餘子皆居禁中。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor's eldest son, Prince of Yun Wen, was without favor and lived in the Sixteen Houses; the other sons all lived within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Prince Wen of Yun, lived unfavored in the Sixteen Houses.

sentences.zh: 夔王滋，第三子也，上愛之，欲以為嗣，為其非次，故久不建東宮。

translations.literal: Prince of Kui Zi, the third son, was beloved; the emperor wished to make him heir, but because it was out of order he long delayed establishing the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He loved third son Zi of Kui but delayed the heir for order of birth.

sentences.zh: 上餌醫官李玄伯、道士虞紫芝、山人王樂藥，疽發於背。

translations.literal: The emperor took drugs from medical officer Li Xuanbo, Daoist Yu Zizhi, and mountain man Wang Leyao; a carbuncle broke out on his back.
translations.idiomatic: Court drugs from Li Xuanbo, Yu Zizhi, and Wang Leyao brought a back abscess.

sentences.zh: 八月，疽甚，宰相及朝臣皆不得見，上密以夔王屬樞密使王歸長、馬公儒、宣徽南院使王居方，使立之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the carbuncle grew severe; chief ministers and court officials could not see him; secretly he entrusted the Prince of Kui to military commissioners Wang Guichang and Ma Gongru and Director of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Wang Jufang to install him.
translations.idiomatic: In eighth month he secretly named Kui prince heir through Wang Guichang and allies.

sentences.zh: 三人及右軍中尉王茂玄，皆上平日所厚也。

translations.literal: The three men and Right Army Commandant Wang Maoxuan were all those the emperor had long favored.
translations.idiomatic: They and Wang Maoxuan were longtime favorites.

sentences.zh: 獨左軍中尉王宗實素不同心，三人相與謀，出宗實為淮南監軍。

translations.literal: Only Left Army Commandant Wang Zongshi had never been of one mind with them; the three plotted to send Zongshi out as Huainan monitor.
translations.idiomatic: They plotted to exile rival eunuch Wang Zongshi to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 宗實已受敕於宣化門外，將自銀台門出。

translations.literal: Zongshi had already received the order outside Xuanhua Gate and was about to exit through Yintai Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zongshi was leaving through Yintai Gate with his order.

sentences.zh: 左軍副使亓元實謂宗實曰：「聖人不豫逾月，中尉止隔門起居，今日除改，未可辨也。

translations.literal: Left Army vice commandant Qi Yuanshi said to Zongshi, "The sage has been unwell more than a month; the commandant has only attended through the gate—today's appointment cannot yet be verified.
translations.idiomatic: “Qi Yuanshi urged Zongshi to see the emperor before leaving.

sentences.zh: 何不見聖人而出！」

translations.literal: Why not see the sage and then go out!"
translations.idiomatic: See the emperor first, he said."

sentences.zh: 宗實感寤，復入，諸門已踵故事增人守捉矣。

translations.literal: Zongshi was moved to clarity and re-entered; at every gate guards had already been increased by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Zongshi turned back; every gate was heavily guarded.

sentences.zh: 亓元實翼導宗實直至寢殿，上已崩，東首環泣矣。

translations.literal: Qi Yuanshi guided Zongshi straight to the sleeping hall; the emperor had already died, and they were weeping east of the head.
translations.idiomatic: They found the emperor dead; attendants wept by the bed.

sentences.zh: 宗實叱歸長等，責以矯詔，皆捧足乞命。

translations.literal: Zongshi rebuked Guichang and the others and charged them with forging the edict; all clutched his feet begging for life.
translations.idiomatic: Zongshi accused them of forging the succession edict.

sentences.zh: 乃遣宣徽北院使齊元簡迎鄆王。

translations.literal: He then sent Director of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Qi Yuanjian to welcome the Prince of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qi Yuanjian to fetch Prince Wen of Yun.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，下詔立鄆王為皇太子，權句當軍國政事，仍更名漼。

translations.literal: On renchen an edict installed the Prince of Yun as heir apparent to handle state affairs and renamed him Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Renchen: Prince Yun became heir Cui.

sentences.zh: 收歸長、公儒、居方，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Guichang, Gongru, and Jufang were arrested and all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Guichang, Gongru, and Jufang were executed.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，宣遺制，以令狐綯攝塚宰。

translations.literal: On guisi the testamentary edict was proclaimed, making Linghu Tao regent for the funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: Guisi: Linghu Tao became funeral regent.

sentences.zh: 宣宗性明察沉斷，用法無私，從諫如流，重惜官賞，恭謹節儉，惠愛民物，故大中之政，訖於唐亡，人思詠之，謂之小太宗。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuānzong was by nature perspicacious, resolute, and strict in applying the law without partiality; he followed remonstrance like a flowing stream, cherished office and rewards, was reverent and frugal, and loved the people—therefore the government of the Dazhong era, down to the fall of Tang, was remembered in song as "little Taizong."
translations.idiomatic: Xuānzong's Dazhong reign was remembered as a small Taizong until Tang's fall.

sentences.zh: 丙申，懿宗即位。

translations.literal: On bingchen Emperor Yizong took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Bingchen: Yizong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，尊皇太后為太皇太后。

translations.literal: On guimao the empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Guimao: the empress dowager became grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 以王宗實為驃騎上將軍。

translations.literal: Wang Zongshi was made General-in-Chief of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongshi became general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 李玄伯、虞紫芝、王樂皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Li Xuanbo, Yu Zizhi, and Wang Leyao were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The physicians and alchemists were executed.

sentences.zh: 九月，追尊上母晁昭容為元昭皇太后。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the emperor's mother, Lady Chao of the Zhaorong rank, was posthumously honored as Grand Empress Dowager Yuanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Lady Chao was honored as Grand Empress Dowager Yuanzhao.

sentences.zh: 加魏博節度使何弘敬兼中書令，幽州節度使張允伸同平章事。

translations.literal: Weibo military commissioner He Hongjing was additionally made Director of the Secretariat; Youzhou military commissioner Zhang Yunshen was made Co-Equal Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He Hongjing gained the secretariat; Zhang Yunshen the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛卯，赦天下。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinmao, an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, xinmao: general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊午，以門下侍郎、同平章事蕭鄴同平章事，充荊南節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuwu, Vice Director of the Gate Bureau and Co-Equal Chief Minister Xiao Ye was made Co-Equal Chief Minister and military commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, wuwu: Xiao Ye went to Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲申，以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎杜審權同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiashen, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War Du Shenquan was made Co-Equal Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, jiashen: Du Shenquan entered the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 審權，元穎之弟孫也。

translations.literal: Shenquan was a younger brother's grandson of Yuan Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shenquan was Yuan Ying's grandnephew.

sentences.zh: 浙東賊帥裘甫攻陷象山，官軍屢敗，明州城門晝閉，進逼剡縣，有眾百人，浙東騷動。
